items.title: Using informatics to understand pediatric allergic diseases
items.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Recent advances in the power, utility, and accessibility of artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled new methods of investigation in the biomedical sciences and opportunities to transform clinical workflows. As allergic conditions are among the most common chronic diseases affecting children, pediatric allergy represents a promising area for AI-augmented informatics methods to support molecular discovery, early identification, risk stratification, treatment customization, and longitudinal monitoring, as reviewed herein. RECENT FINDINGS: Recent pediatric allergy studies have applied informatics and AI methodologies across various data sources, including molecular and multiomic data, structured and unstructured electronic health record data, environmental exposures, diagnostic images, remote monitoring devices, and patient- and clinician-facing AI tools. Primarily still in the research phase, these approaches include biomarker discovery, disease phenotyping, risk stratification, prediction modeling, remote monitoring, and emerging chatbots for allergy education. SUMMARY: Although still relatively nascent within pediatric allergy, AI-augmented informatics shows promise for extracting usable information from complex data and developing tools aimed at personalizing disease detection and management. Most applications remain investigational, and continued progress will require transparency, rigorous validation, generalizability across diverse populations and health systems, feasibility of workflow integration, privacy protection, and longitudinal oversight to ensure continued safety and effectiveness.

items.title: Viewpoint on Neural Mechanisms for Multisensory Integration in Speech Perception
items.abstract: Abstract This interview brings together perspectives from the authors on the origins, evolution, and future directions of multisensory neuroscience. The authors reflect on their early motivations, tracing the field’s development from studies of intersensory attention and early cortical integration to contemporary investigations of naturalistic audiovisual speech. They highlight landmark empirical and methodological advances — including high-density EEG, BOLD fMRI, intracranial recordings, and analyses of continuous stimuli — that overturned the traditional view of multisensory integration as a strictly higher-order process. Central themes include the role of the superior temporal sulcus in audiovisual speech, the hierarchical and temporally dynamic nature of multisensory binding, and ongoing debates concerning the mechanisms underlying neural responses to naturalistic stimuli, such as evoked-response versus oscillatory-entrainment accounts. The interview also addresses current controversies, including interpretations of redundant signals effects and the neural organization of language, as well as concerns about underpowered studies and reproducibility. The authors strongly advocate open science practices, emphasizing data and code sharing while acknowledging structural challenges. Looking ahead, they discuss the transformative potential of artificial intelligence, invasive human recordings, genetic models, and translational applications, particularly for neurodevelopmental disorders. Collectively, this dialogue situates multisensory integration as a rapidly advancing field bridging sensory processing, cognition, and clinical relevance.

items.title: Virology-aware artificial intelligence for respiratory antiviral discovery: from molecular docking biases to RdRp-centered benchmarking
items.abstract: Respiratory RNA viruses remain a persistent threat because they combine high transmissibility, rapid evolution, immune escape, zoonotic spillover, and incomplete therapeutic coverage. RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRps) and polymerase complexes are among the most conserved and pharmacologically actionable viral targets, yet they are also challenging computational targets because their ligandable states depend on RNA templates, cofactors, divalent metals, multidomain architecture, and conformational transitions. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), geometric deep learning (GDL), and generative molecular design are increasingly used to accelerate antiviral discovery, yet their performance is often inferred from general protein-ligand benchmarks dominated by non-viral targets. This review argues that respiratory RNA virus polymerases are a high-value but comparatively underrepresented class of antiviral targets and a complementary test case for evaluating AI-guided drug discovery. We synthesize current approaches in computer-aided drug design (CADD), molecular docking, ML-assisted virtual screening, molecular representations, pose-generation models, generative AI, and protein-ligand affinity benchmarking. We emphasize that docking scores, predicted affinity, and root-mean-square error (RMSE) values are insufficient unless linked to target engagement, enzymatic inhibition, cell-based antiviral activity, cytotoxicity, resistance, and pharmacological feasibility. We propose an RdRp-centered AI pipeline that integrates curated polymerase structural ensembles, leakage-resistant benchmarking, antiviral-specific evaluation tasks, ADME/Tox filtering, biochemical validation, cell-based infection assays, resistance profiling, and iterative model refinement. Moving beyond docking scores requires benchmarking models under virologically realistic conditions and validating whether computational prioritization enriches compounds with experimentally actionable antiviral activity.

items.title: VisualTrust: Video Reasoning under On-Screen Claim Framing
items.abstract: On-screen text can describe what a video shows, or it can frame what the video is supposed to mean. Current benchmarks treat both alike, testing whether a model can read the text rather than whether it should trust it. We study claim deference, multimodal large language models' tendency to let an on-screen claim override conflicting visual evidence. We introduce VisualTrust, a counterfactual benchmark with 5,063 cases across 14 claim-fact classes. Each case pairs a question with three versions of the same video: one with no claim, one with an accurate claim, and one with a misleading claim that alters a single grounded fact. The option the misleading claim supports is the trap answer. Across seven open-weight and four proprietary models, mean accuracy falls from 90.1% without a claim to 51.9% with a misleading claim. Among initially correct responses, 42.8% flip to the trap answer and only 0.6% become other errors. Strong no-claim accuracy does not ensure resistance. We also introduce DEAR (Decoupled Evidence Arbitration and Reading), a training-free agent for video question answering that separates evidence arbitration from reading. An independent check reports conflicting evidence, a selector weighs it without a fixed modality priority and blinds what it withholds, and the reader answers from the resulting video in a fresh context. On 500 videos across three proprietary models, DEAR raises accuracy under misleading claims from 47.2--64.0% to 81.8--85.2% and reduces trap-answer selection from 34.4--50.8% to 11.6--15.0%, while preserving no-claim accuracy.

items.title: VoxTurn: Answering Several Turn-Taking Questions in One Pass with One Model
items.abstract: A cascaded voice agent must decide, throughout each silence of its user, whether the user has finished their turn: answering too early cuts the user off, answering too late makes the agent slow. It often needs related decisions too: will the user soon go on, is speech during its own turn an interruption or a backchannel, is a sound speech at all. With open detectors, each extra decision costs another model or another call, and on the 14-language eot-bench they cut users off in more than a quarter of mid-turn pauses. Because they are trained on segmented utterances, this mismatch is the largest single source of error. We present VoxTurn, a 0.8B speech LLM that casts these decisions as multiple-choice questions, scores the hidden state of each option, and answers any set of them in one forward pass with a block-isolating attention mask, exactly as if asked one at a time. Trained on real conversational pauses with labels derived from their timing, and re-queried while a silence lasts, VoxTurn reaches 11.5% false cut-offs in English at a 300 ms latency budget, comparable to two commercial detectors, and a 14-language mean of 19.9%, the lowest among open models, at 8.3 ms per decision. In Pipecat and LiveKit it cuts off 17% and 9% of turns, and it ranks fifth of 24 in TurnBench end-of-turn detection without any TurnBench training data. The model, code and framework plugins are released.

items.title: WebMCP: A Browser-Native navigator.modelContext Standard for Agentic Web Automation
items.abstract: Purpose: This paper examines WebMCP, a proposed browser-native web platform standard that lets websites expose explicit, schema-described tools to large language model agents, as an alternative to actuation, in which an agent simulates the clicks, keystrokes, and navigation a human would perform. Methodology: The paper analyzes WebMCP, incubated within the World Wide Web Consortium's Web Machine Learning Community Group and implemented as an origin trial in the Chrome browser beginning with Chrome 149. We describe WebMCP's architecture, including the browser-mediated JavaScript interface navigator.modelContext and a declarative HTML annotation form, and its relationship to Anthropic's Model Context Protocol; analyze its security and permission model; place it within a comparative design-space taxonomy alongside DOM automation, computer-use agents, and server-side Model Context Protocol integrations; and examine the emerging standardization landscape, including browser vendor positions and adjacent efforts such as the Agentic Commerce Protocol. A generalized use case illustrates how a composite retail website might expose search, filtering, and checkout tools under this model. All sources and data referenced in this manuscript are dated on or before June 30, 2026. Findings: WebMCP allows a website to register tools that an agent invokes directly rather than inferring actions from pixels or DOM structure, with a security model built on origin isolation, a dedicated Permissions Policy directive, and a human-in-the-loop confirmation mechanism for consequential actions. Open problems remain in cross-site tool discovery, adversarial tool poisoning, and the evaluation of agent-web interaction quality. Unique Contribution to Theory, Policy and Practice: For theory, the paper contributes a comparative design-space taxonomy that positions browser-native, declarative agent integration against actuation-based and server-side approaches. For practice, it gives web developers and agent builders a technical account of WebMCP's registration mechanisms, security model, and interaction flow. For policy, it informs browser vendors and standards bodies through its analysis of the standardization landscape and a research agenda for browser-native agent integration standards as this area continues to develop.

items.title: What do AI chatbots do after users decline therapeutic redirection for suicide thoughts?
items.abstract: Safety evaluations of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots focus on therapeutic redirection, statements urging users who disclose suicide thoughts to seek help from crisis lines or other human sources. How chatbots respond when users refuse that help is unclear. This cross-sectional audit ran 2,550 scripted multi-turn conversations in September 2026. Each conversation opened with a disclosure of suicide thoughts at 3 levels of severity, answered every referral with up to 10 standardized refusals and then changed the subject. All 2,550 conversations included a referral, 2,542 (99.7%) in the first reply. However, mean persistence ranged from 0.01 to 9.94 refusals across chatbots. Newer versions of all 5 chatbots tested in 2 versions persisted less than older versions (each P < .05). Compared with passive ideation, a disclosure of intent was associated with 1.26 more refusals sustained (95% CI, 1.06-1.46) and higher odds of renewed referral after the topic change (odds ratio, 10.07; 95% CI, 7.43-13.66). Chatbots that persisted less in referral more often presented themselves as the user's support (Spearman rho = -0.80; P < .001). Of 8,818 refusal-phase replies urging outside help, only 173 (2.0%) asked about barriers to seeking it. Chatbots uniformly recommended outside help after disclosures of suicide thoughts but varied widely in persisting in those recommendations, with newer versions persisting less. Safety evaluations should test what happens after a crisis referral is refused, not only whether one is offered.

items.title: What Is Left for Us?
items.abstract: ABSTRACT We argue that generative AI can degrade research by eroding the very practices through which scholarly judgement is formed. As constitutive conditions for the production and validation of knowledge, these practices cannot be reduced to the outputs of research, which is what AI tools so effectively simulate. When scholars delegate central tasks of inquiry to large language models (LLMs), they may stop engaging in these practices and lose the formation they provide: The output may improve while the researcher fails to develop. Against this risk, merely keeping humans ‘in the loop’ as prompters or quality‐checkers of AI outputs is insufficient to preserve research as a site of intellectual formation. What is needed instead is a renewed commitment to research as a lived practice in which judgement is formed gradually, often through friction, and participation in a scholarly community. We defend it because it rests on four sources and warrants of research that cannot be automated: tacit knowledge, personal commitment, socialisation and deep reading. These enact what we call ‘second scholarship,’ that is, the reappropriation of scholarly craft, chosen out of a critical experience of what AI tools can and cannot do. Researchers who practise it may delegate tasks to these tools, provided that their own judgement in the delegated competence is already formed, that they can answer for the output and that they keep exercising the competence themselves. What cannot and should not be delegated becomes what research communities must value and answer for. This is what is left for us.

items.title: What It Is, Not What It Says: Securing Agentic Browsing Interactions with Web Semantics
items.abstract: AI agents increasingly browse the web on users' behalf, yet they consume webpages as screenshots or text, exposing their LLMs to unvetted third-party content. Browsers enforce semantics under which what an element can do depends on what it is and where it comes from, not on what it says. Agents flatten these semantics, so injected text can persuade the LLM to exercise the user's authority for content that has none. As LLMs remain easy to persuade, the agent's interface to the web must itself ensure the integrity of what the agent reads, interprets, and does. We propose Intact, which runs on an unmodified browser. Intact builds GenTree, a bespoke representation that captures provenance and web semantics. Intact passes the page via GenTree to the LLM one element at a time, so the LLM decides on each element without any other element's text. Its harness executes each step only within the capabilities of the step's element and asks the user before acting on third-party content. On 1,270 real webpages, GenTree attributes 2.3x as many elements to third parties as the browser, which misattributes 58.7% of them to the first party. On 1,091 of these webpages with injected attacks, only 12.8% of attacks get through Intact's planner, each at most as a consent request, against 73.1% for a conventional planner. Isolation disrupts functionality on only 3.7% of tasks, and a parallel schedule could remove most of its added latency.

items.title: What matters in medical training in Wales: a thematic analysis of Wales-specific responses to the NHS England Medical Training Review Call for Evidence
items.abstract: Abstract Background Postgraduate medical education in the United Kingdom is delivered within health services experiencing sustained workforce shortages, workload pressure, and reduced supervisory capacity. National evidence has highlighted concerns around staffing, burnout, training quality, flexibility, and progression, but Wales-specific qualitative synthesis remains limited. This study aimed to identify and interpret key themes arising from the Wales-specific responses to the NHS England Medical Training Review Phase 1 Call for Evidence and to situate these findings in relation to wider UK medical education and workforce evidence. Methods This qualitative study used thematic analysis of Wales-specific free-text responses from the NHS England Medical Training Review Phase 1 Call for Evidence. The dataset comprised responses from 133 respondents who identified with, or commented on, the Welsh medical training context. Analysis involved inductive coding within the broad question-led domains of the parent survey and drew on reflexive principles. Findings were compared at the theme level with the broader Medical Training Review Call for Evidence summary and General Medical Council State of Medical Education and Practice workplace evidence. Results Eleven cross-cutting themes were identified: training capacity and workforce pressures; recruitment, progression, and career development; geographical stability and flexibility; training quality, supervision, and protected educational time; workload, wellbeing, and flexibility; equity and inclusion; curriculum modernisation; service-training conflict; community and interface training; digital infrastructure and artificial intelligence; and system-level reform. The strongest alignment with broader evidence concerned workforce capacity, supervision constraints, service pressure, and structural reform. Wales-specific responses added contextual depth by showing how these pressures were experienced in relation to place-based retention, progression from non-training roles, and the displacement of training by service demand. Conclusions Wales-specific responses to the NHS England Medical Training Review indicate that concerns about medical training in Wales are closely connected to wider UK workforce and training pressures yet shaped by the Welsh service and workforce context. Reform should address training capacity, workforce planning, protected educational time, equitable progression, flexibility, and sustainable working conditions as interdependent features of postgraduate medical education.

items.abstract: AI can improve the quality and speed of work without establishing whether people are developing the judgement needed to examine evidence, recognise omissions and respond appropriately when circumstances change. This whitepaper examines how AI can remove, enrich or relocate the experiences through which judgement develops. Drawing on research into workplace learning, expertise, AI-assisted performance and human oversight, it distinguishes assisted output from retained understanding and transferable judgement. The paper connects Capability Design and Capability Leadership with Human Judgement Assurance (HJA), proposed as an approach to establishing justified confidence through evidence of development, competent appraisal, effective intervention and sustained capability. It explains HJA’s boundaries and relationship with AI Assurance and Capability Assurance. Leaders, educators and practitioners are invited to begin with one consequential workflow and examine how judgement develops, operates and is renewed. items.title: When AI Gives the Feedback: Evaluative Outsourcing and Learner Agency in the English Writing Classroom
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used to provide feedback and support revision in English writing. Existing debate has largely examined the quality, accuracy, and effectiveness of AI-generated feedback. This conceptual paper argues that such concerns risk overlooking a more fundamental pedagogical issue: the redistribution of evaluative work between learner and system. Drawing on feedback literacy and evaluative judgement, the paper introduces evaluative outsourcing to describe the delegation of interpretive, judgemental, and decision-making work in feedback engagement to AI. It argues that GenAI can enable substantial textual improvement while requiring limited learner participation in the evaluation underlying revision, creating an AI feedback paradox in which better revision does not necessarily indicate better judgement. The paper proposes four principles for retaining learner evaluative agency: making evaluative decisions visible, designing for comparison, preserving consequential decisions for learners, and creating opportunities for evaluative transfer.

items.title: When CONTRIBUTING Files Fall Short: Revising OSS Contribution Guidelines with Repository Evidence
items.abstract: Contribution guidelines help newcomers participate in open-source software projects, yet often contain incomplete or outdated information. Existing studies characterize newcomers' information needs and documentation gaps, but revising these guidelines requires recovering and validating project-specific knowledge from scattered sources. We present ContribAlign, a framework for automatically revising CONTRIBUTING files through category-guided evidence integration. A qualitative analysis yields a taxonomy of 30 fine-grained guidance types across six contribution categories. ContribAlign uses a classifier to diagnose coverage of the six categories in the original guidance, then uses the taxonomy to collect and organize project-specific evidence. It filters detected conflicts and uses a large language model to generate category-level revisions. The classifier achieves a weighted F1 score of 0.764, improving on the existing classifier by 0.156, while the verifier detects factual conflicts with 97.3% precision and 91.5% estimated recall. Human evaluation shows that ContribAlign achieves the highest overall quality among the original guidelines and three baselines, with significant improvements in usefulness, beginner-friendliness, and completeness. These results suggest that ContribAlign can help maintain more accurate and useful contribution guidelines.

items.title: When is a better LLM worth paying for? Stochastic Optimization with Switching Mixed-Fidelity Oracles
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used upstream of decision-making to clean data, detect label errors, and reconstruct missing values. Yet LLM-assisted data curation creates a new operational tradeoff: higher-fidelity models and richer prompts can be substantially more expensive, while the value of this additional fidelity depends on the downstream optimization accuracy. This raises the central question of this work: when should one pay for a better LLM, given a specific downstream task at hand? We study this question through stochastic optimization with mixed-fidelity first-order oracles, which can have systematic bias and state-dependent variance. We develop two cost-aware algorithmic frameworks that allow adaptive switching between stochastic oracles. With known bias, the first meta-algorithm applies a restarted, cost-aware policy that adaptively selects oracle fidelity across optimization stages. Its cumulative cost is no larger than that of the best fixed oracle in hindsight and can be substantially smaller. With unknown bias, we develop a budgeted certification scheme that uses occasional trusted-gradient evaluations to certify the optimization progress and eliminate unsuccessful oracle sources, and show an explicit tradeoff between certification cost and delayed detection of biased sources. We provide concrete realizations of these meta-algorithms by applying biased stochastic gradient extrapolation (SGE) and recursive regularization under state-dependent noise as subroutines. Synthetic and LLM-completion experiments illustrate the qualitative switching behavior predicted by the theory: the adaptive policy skips several expensive LLM oracles and substantially reduces cumulative cost relative to fixed high-fidelity alternatives while achieving comparable accuracy.

items.title: When Reasoning Is Not Enough: Proactive Inquiry for Cross-Modal Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can act unsafely when individually benign images and texts are interpreted jointly. Beyond implicit reasoning risk, where reasoning drifts toward harm, we identify intent-level risk, where cross-modal ambiguity silently commits the model to a hazardous premise that path-level optimization alone cannot correct. We propose SAFE-PRO, which uses a Risk-Conditioned Uncertainty (RCU) signal, combining predictive entropy with a learned cross-modal risk score, to decide when to ask safety-grounded clarifying questions and where to apply path optimization, under a reward that prioritizes safety and penalizes over-refusal. We also build SSUI-Dialog, a multimodal multi-turn dataset with dual-intent supervision, and theoretically analyze gradient variance and unsafe-completion risk under RCU. Across seven benchmarks and two base MLLMs, SAFE-PRO consistently improves safety over SRPO, roughly halves its over-refusal, and surpasses GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet in average single-turn safety.

items.title: Where Does the AI Time Dividend Go? Generative AI, Work Intensification, and Work-Life Balance
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can accelerate knowledge-work tasks, but task-level efficiency does not necessarily translate into shorter working hours or improved employee welfare. This article proposes an AI time-dividend allocation framework that separates the creation of saved time from its subsequent use. Drawing on the job demands–resources perspective, it examines a resource pathway through perceived time savings and work–life balance alongside a competing demand pathway through work intensification. The reported three-wave observational survey comprises 472 complete cases. Standardized ordinary least squares models with HC3 robust standard errors indicate that GenAI use intensity is associated with perceived time savings (β = .495, p < .001). Time savings is positively associated with work–life balance (β = .255, p < .001), whereas work intensification is negatively associated with work–life balance (β = −.443, p < .001). Reported bootstrap indirect effects are positive through time savings (0.126, 95% CI [0.079, 0.176]) and negative through time savings and work intensification (−0.036, 95% CI [−0.059, −0.015]). Performance pressure is positively associated with intensification, but its proposed interaction with time savings is not statistically significant. The findings are consistent with competing allocation pathways; given the observational design, they should not be interpreted as causal effects. The article identifies time-dividend allocation as a consequential dimension of AI-enabled work design.

items.title: Who Oversees the Systems That Oversee Us?
items.abstract: Paper 1 of 2 in the AI Governance & Accountability Dossier. As AI shapes decisions about benefits, work, housing, credit, education and information, this paper asks who can inspect a system, challenge its use, and require a remedy. It reviews the 2025-26 U.S. governance landscape, including the GAO requirement count, OMB M-25-21 and M-25-22, Executive Order 14365 and state activity, and separates rules from remedies. It proposes a six-question diagnostic (authority, responsibility, evidence, visibility, challenge, remedy), a Minimum Accountability Package that works without a new office, and a comparison of three institutional models, including an elected state-level commissioner with independent technical staff. It treats the human-factors evidence as narrow, states what would change its conclusions, and labels every material claim in a ledger as documented, reported, interpretation or hypothesis. items.title: WORK ENVIRONMENT, WORK SUPERVISION, JOB TRAINING, AND OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND SAFETY FOR CONSTRUCTION WORK PRODUCTIVITY
items.abstract: This study examines the effects of work environment, work supervision, and job training on occupational safety and health (K3) and work productivity, as well as the effect of K3 on work productivity among 200 employees at CV Griya Fajar Konstruksi, South Tangerang. A quantitative approach was employed using survey data from 200 employees and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The results show that work environment and work supervision have positive and statistically significant effects on K3 and work productivity, while K3 has the strongest positive relationship with work productivity (β = 0.989; p < 0.001). In contrast, job training shows negative and statistically significant relationships with K3 (β = −0.437; p = 0.034) and work productivity (β = −0.285; p = 0.041). Five of the seven hypotheses are supported. The findings qualify the expected positive role of training by indicating that its provision alone does not necessarily translate into improved safety and productivity. The findings also highlight the importance of integrating supportive working conditions, consistent supervision, effective K3 practices, and relevant and practical training to support safe and productive construction operations.

items.title: Workplace Safety Judgment from Images: Comparing AI Assistants Across Five Occupational Contexts
items.abstract: This study compared the image-based workplace safety judgments of three general-purpose AI assistants across five occupational contexts. Fifteen workplace images representing construction, workshop/manufacturing, maintenance/technical service, warehouse/logistics, and laboratory settings were evaluated by ChatGPT GPT-5.5, Claude Sonnet 5, and Gemini 3.5 Flash. Each model completed 15 single-image assessments and five within-context relative-ranking tasks, yielding 60 outputs. Two occupational safety specialists independently rated the outputs on five 0–5 dimensions and six binary error patterns. The raters showed exact or near-exact score agreement in 81.8% of the ordinal ratings; pooled quadratic weighted agreement was moderate, κ = 0.479, 95% CI [0.340, 0.595]. Agreement was complete for pairwise ranking accuracy and exact final ordering. Based on the two-rater means, ChatGPT led in visible evidence coverage (4.37), visual fidelity (4.43), prioritization (3.73), and uncertainty discipline (4.70), whereas Claude obtained the highest descriptive control-guidance mean (4.40). Between-model differences were statistically significant in the other four dimensions but not in control guidance. No rater-confirmed problematic control recommendation was observed. All three models achieved the same final-match performance: four of five context rankings were fully correct and 14 of 15 pairwise relations were correct. The shared failure occurred in the workshop/manufacturing context, where the image containing a visible person at height was ranked below a dusty but static scene. The findings support supervised first-pass use of AI assistants but not autonomous workplace safety evaluation.

items.title: Workplace Spirituality and Workplace Thriving Moderated Mediation of Intrinsic Motivation and Work Meaningfulness among Secondary School Teachers in Nigeria
items.abstract: This study examines the relationships among intrinsic motivation, workplace thriving, and spirituality among teachers in Nigeria. The researchers collected data from 399 teachers and analysed the data using structural equation modelling with SmartPLS 3 and SPSS. The results showed that workplace spirituality was positively and strongly associated with workplace thriving, while intrinsic motivation was also significantly associated with workplace thriving. Further analysis showed that the work meaningfulness mediated the relationship between workplace spirituality and workplace thriving. In addition, the interaction between workplace spirituality and intrinsic motivation significantly influenced workplace thriving. The findings highlight the importance of workplace spirituality, intrinsic motivation, and work meaningfulness in promoting workplace thriving among secondary school teachers. Important practical implications are presented.

items.abstract: Series: A Plaine and Easie Introduction to Digital Music Scholarship (Workshop 2 of 5), The University of Melbourne, 27 August – 1 October 2026About this workshopIn this workshop we’ll take a look at an important archive of concert programs and memorabilia that document concert life in twentieth-century Melbourne, now part of the Rare Music Collection here at the University. It is a vast resource—over a hundred boxes covering not only orchestral, choral, and chamber concerts, but theater, ballet, jazz, too. To date, the only way into the collection is via a 300-page typescript summary. While this is a helpful guide, it hardly provides scholars and librarians with the control they need to explore the riches within. In this workshop, we will show how new digital tools (including Large Language Models) can help us extract structured data from the guide—and tell hidden stories about the people, spaces, and music of Melbourne’s past.With the assistance of Holden Starkey (Haverford College Class of 2027).Thursday 3 September 2026, Room 721, Building 880, The University of Melbourne.Slides: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1HSUVoYI0--jTYCSTDefQpxCtHZEGgctF6UxSdQPCMSk/edit Workshop page (data, code and other materials): https://sites.google.com/haverford.edu/melbourne2026workshops/hidden-history-melbourneAbout the seriesThis is one of a series of five workshops organized by Professor Richard Freedman (Haverford College, USA), in collaboration with Dr. Daniel Russo-Batterham (MDAP, Melbourne University) and Dr. Nick Tochka (Department of Music, Melbourne University). items.title: Writing Motivation and Self‐Efficacy in AI ‐Chatbot‐Supported EFL Writing: Exploratory Insights Across Proficiency Levels
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Writing motivation and self‐efficacy are critical factors of success in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) contexts, yet they are frequently undermined by learner anxiety and limited teacher feedback. While artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots offer potential for adaptive writing support, limited research has examined these affective constructs in parallel across learner proficiency levels. Objectives This study investigated changes in intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and writing self‐efficacy among high school EFL learners at higher‐ and lower‐proficiency levels following chatbot‐supported writing and examined whether these changes differed across proficiency levels. Methods Using an exploratory mixed‐methods design, the study involved 47 Vietnamese high school students divided into higher‐ and lower‐proficiency level groups. Over the 11‐week study, participants completed 8 weeks of AI‐supported writing activities using a chatbot designed in accordance with principles of Self‐Determination Theory, Self‐Regulated Learning Theory and Self‐Efficacy Theory. Changes in intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and writing self‐efficacy were examined using pre‐ and post‐questionnaires and semi‐structured interviews. Results and Conclusions The quantitative findings revealed that intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and writing self‐efficacy increased over time in both proficiency groups, with no significant differences in the magnitude of change between higher‐ and lower‐proficiency learners. This suggests that the affective changes observed during AI‐supported writing were not confined to one proficiency group. The qualitative findings indicated that learners linked their positive experiences to reduced anxiety, clearer guidance, and supportive interaction, although the types of support they valued differed by proficiency level. Overall, the findings suggest that when positioned as a supportive writing partner rather than an answer generator, AI chatbot feedback may be associated with positive motivational and self‐efficacy development in mixed‐ability EFL writing classrooms.

items.title: XAI-SFD: an explainable artificial intelligence framework for intelligent digitalisation of shit flow diagrams and smart sanitation management in South Africa
items.abstract: Despite the availability of safe sanitation access, this issue remains a major challenge in many developing nations like South Africa where there are challenges associated with the fragmented data gathering, manual reporting, and lack of interoperability and real-time monitoring of the sanitation service chain. Shit Flow Diagrams (SFDs) are among the tools that can be used for the presentation and analysis of the sanitation service chain as well as identification of potential risks in the sanitation systems; however, the creation of traditional SFDs is a manual process and leaves no space for continuous monitoring. This paper proposes XAI-SFD, an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI)-based solution for the intelligent digitalization of Shit Flow Diagrams (SFDs) and smart sanitation management in South Africa. This approach is based on IoT data gathering, GIS-based spatial analysis, data validation, machine learning, explainable artificial intelligence, sanitation service chain modelling, Digital Twin technology and dashboard decision-making support. Explainability provides transparency and allows the stakeholders to understand what influences the risk assessment and prioritization. A proof-of-concept was carried out on a controlled municipality scale, using 247 monitoring stations of the Routine Inland Water Quality Monitoring network of the City of Cape Town. A total of four clusters of spatial contexts were identified, with the selected clustering model providing a silhouette coefficient of 0.3133 and Davies-Bouldin index of 1.3324. As a result of the explained priority assessment, 25 monitoring stations (10.12%) have been defined as belonging to the high-priority class, 99 stations (40.08%) belonging to the medium-priority class, and 123 stations (49.80%) belonging to the low-priority class. Because of the lack of sanitation flows outcomes and water quality monitoring results in the dataset on monitoring sites, it is possible to consider the results received as prototyping findings and not as the validation of sanitation risk prediction models. In this regard, the proposed XAI-SFD architecture may be used as the base for further creation of heterogeneous databases of sanitation and environmental data.

items.title: XARA: A Multimodal Agentic System for eXtended Reality Experiment Generation
items.abstract: Controlled experiments are essential for advancing transportation research, yet designing eXtended Reality (XR) environments for behavioural studies remains technically demanding and inaccessible to many domain researchers. Current workflows require proficiency in game engines such as Unity or Unreal Engine, imposing significant barriers to rapid scenario prototyping and iterative experiment design. This paper presents XARA, a novel system that integrates a dual large language model (LLM) architecture with an immersive XR environment to enable voice driven experiment generation for transportation research. XARA employs a pipeline in which spoken natural language commands are first transcribed and then interpreted into structured commands that manipulate a Unity based XR scene in real time. The system supports object creation, spatial manipulation, animation control, and scene persistence through a modular architecture. By lowering the technical threshold for XR experiment creation, XARA enables transportation researchers to rapidly prototype driving, pedestrian, and urban design scenarios using intuitive voice commands and hand gestures within an immersive 3D environment. This paper describes the system architecture, the voice to command pipeline, and discusses potential applications across behavioural travel experiments, safety studies, human factors research, and policy testing.

items.abstract: Данное исследование посвящено актуальной теме структурной трансформации экономики, вызванной внедрением передовых ИТ-решений и развитием систем искусственного интеллекта. Рассмотрена взаимосвязь между достижениями в ИТ-секторе и изменениями структуры отраслей вследствие снижения издержек при внедрении ИТ и повышения скорости и качества принятия решений. Выявлены ключевые драйверы технологических изменений, определяющие темпы отраслевой адаптации, а также обозначены некоторые последствия цифрового неравенства. Отмечены такие тенденции, как возникновение новых рыночных сегментов и изменение роли человеческого капитала в условиях технологических сдвигов. Проведенный анализ подтверждает инфраструктурное значение ИТ: происходит переход бизнеса от модели реакции на событие к модели предиктивного управления. This study addresses the topical issue of the structural transformation of the economy driven by the implementation of advanced IT solutions and the development of artificial intelligence systems. The relationship between achievements in the IT sector and changes in industrial structures – driven by reduced costs associated with IT implementation and improved speed and quality of decision-making is examined. The key drivers of technological change determining the pace of industry adaptation have been identified, and certain consequences of the digital divide have been outlined. Trends such as the emergence of new market segments and the changing role of human capital amidst technological shifts have been noted. The analysis confirms the infrastructural importance of IT: business is shifting from an event-reactive model to a predictive management model.

items.abstract: Ergonomics in the field of occupational safety is a scientific discipline that focuses on ensuring comfortable and safe working conditions. It studies the interaction between people, technology, and the environment, aiming to adapt workplaces to employees’ physical and cognitive capabilities. The primary goal of ergonomics is to protect workers’ health, reduce fatigue, and improve the safety and efficiency of the work process. Research in this field is aimed at creating safe, comfortable, and highly efficient working conditions. This helps preserve workers’ health and increase their productivity. Ergonomics views people, technology, and the environment as a single system; analyzes the work process through the sequence of an operator’s actions, goals, and tasks; adapts equipment and furniture to human anatomy; and studies fatigue and the strain on the nervous system and the senses. This scientific article analyzes occupational ergonomics as an interdisciplinary science that studies human interaction with the work environment to improve efficiency, safety, and comfort. The term “ergonomics” was coined by Wojciech Jastrzębski in the 19th century, while in the 20th century, this discipline evolved into an independent science due to industrial and military demands following World War II. Current trends include adapting to digitalization, automation, and remote work, highlighting the importance of cognitive ergonomics and human-machine interaction. The economic aspect underscores the cost-effectiveness of ergonomic solutions: reducing injuries and absenteeism, as well as increasing productivity, leads to savings in labor costs. The article offers practical recommendations, such as personalizing workstations and applying modern technologies, and identifies areas for further research on integrating ergonomic principles into cutting-edge technologies, particularly virtual reality and artificial intelligence.

items.abstract: The modern pace of life causes a high demand for anatomically functional footwear. Such products are adapted to the natural biomechanics of the lower extremities, ensure the physiologically correct position of the foot and optimize load distribution. Such footwear minimizes fatigue, prevents the appearance of edema and deformations, which is critically important for people with prolonged static or dynamic activity. At the same time, the consumer places high demands not only on ergonomics, but also on aesthetics and the reproduction of style in the design of products. The study systematizes the theoretical principles of designing anatomically functional footwear with an emphasis on grunge style. Its specific constructive and model parameters are determined. The sequence of the technological process of creating prototypes in compliance with design and utilitarian requirements is clearly demonstrated. The scientific and practical toolkit includes content analysis of the initial data, modeling and anthropometric modernization of the shoe insole elements. The idea of embodying elements of the grunge style in footwear became possible due to: the use of non-standard materials, finishing finished products (finishing with color), the use of insoles with a filled toe part, the implementation of creative design solutions and non-traditional technological approaches in the manufacture of individual elements and parts of footwear (sole, heel) and the assembly of products. The practical implementation of the project was carried out through individual modeling on the basis of the production facilities of Litini LLC. Based on the results obtained, a limited series of products was manufactured, which successfully passed a 60-day operational testing directly by the customer. Experimental wearing confirmed the reliability, comfort and ergonomics of the developed designs in combination with an expressive visual concept. A full set of design and technological support for the designed line was formed.

Цель исследования — изучение специфики рынка социально вредных товаров и услуг и разработка алгоритма его регулирования, направленного на формирование комплексной стратегии, включающей: снижение спроса за счёт информационной работы, просвещения и профилактических программ; ограничение предложения через контроль доступности и регулирование оборота; смягчение ущерба для здоровья населения за счёт мер защиты и поддержки; минимизацию социально-экономических последствий, связанных с потреблением таких товаров и услуг. В рамках исследования проведена разработка языковой программной модели, которая связывает ключевые индикаторы для оценки и прогнозирования в сфере вредных товаров и услуг. Модель позволит: оценивать уровень опасности товаров и услуг, а также их безопасность, прогнозировать риски аварий и уровень токсичности, использовать методы искусственного интеллекта для анализа данных и поддержки принятия решений. The market of socially harmful goods is a multifaceted problem that requires a systematic approach that combines measures of state control, education of citizens and prevention of negative consequences. The purpose of the study is to study the specifics of this market and develop an algorithm for regulating it in order to form a comprehensive strategy that includes: reducing demand through information work, education and preventive programs; limiting supply by controlling accessibility and regulating turnover; mitigating damage to public health by implementing protection and support measures; minimizing socio-economic consequences associated with consumption of these goods and services. As part of this research, a software language model was developed to link key indicators for evaluating and forecasting harmful goods and services. The model will allow you to assess the level of danger of goods and services, as well as their safety, predict the risks of accidents and the level of toxicity, and use artificial intelligence methods to analyze data and support decision-making. This approach will provide a scientifically sound basis for regulating the market and reducing its negative impact on society.

items.abstract: This article examines socio-psychological factors associated with school students’ cognitive activity. It discusses family support, teacher–student interaction, peer relationships, learning motivation, and classroom psychological climate. The aim is to identify and systematize the main factors through theoretical analysis. The study uses comparison and synthesis of scientific literature. Drawing on Vygotsky’s sociocultural theory, Bandura’s social cognitive theory, and Deci and Ryan’s self-determination theory, the article outlines conditions that may support students’ cognitive engagement. No experimental data are reported. The theoretical conclusions may inform psychological and pedagogical practices in schools.

items.abstract: The article examines the development of critical thinking among students in grades 5–6 through solving non-routine mathematical problems. It explores the potential of such problems to develop logical reasoning, information analysis, hypothesis formation, contradiction detection, and the ability to justify solutions. The article analyzes the solution methods for six problems based on logical tables, the method of assumption, combinatorial analysis, periodicity, and parity. The use of these tasks in mathematics lessons aims to enhance students’ cognitive engagement, foster independent thinking, and develop their ability to formulate well-founded conclusions.

items.abstract: The transition to the digital era has significantly enhanced the efficiency of navigational systems and maritime management. At the same time, however, it has increased the vulnerability of maritime infrastructure to cyber threats, particularly signal spoofing and signal jamming. These threats can undermine the reliability and integrity of positioning, navigation, communication, and maritime situational awareness systems, all of which are critical to the protection of national maritime interests. This article aims to analyze the characteristics, mechanisms, and strategic implications of signal spoofing and signal jamming within the broader context of maritime cybersecurity. The study employs a qualitative documentary analysis of relevant strategic and legal frameworks, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea 1982, Thailand’s National Maritime Security Plan 2023–2027, and the Maritime National Interest Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019). The findings indicated that the integration of multidimensional information through a Multi-Domain Awareness framework, together with the establishment of a Maritime Cyber Command and the development of a Maritime Cyber Intelligence system, would significantly strengthen national capabilities to detect, prevent, respond to, and recover from maritime cyber threats in a systematic and coordinated manner. Such measures would enhance maritime security resilience, protect critical maritime infrastructure, and safeguard the continuity and stability of national maritime interests. The article therefore argues that maritime cybersecurity should be elevated from a predominantly technical concern to a strategic national security priority. An integrated institutional framework, supported by intelligence fusion, interagency coordination, technological capability development, and clearly defined command-and-control mechanisms, is essential for maintaining maritime security and strategic stability amid a rapidly evolving and increasingly complex security environment.

items.abstract: This qualitative descriptive study aimed to explore the self-management experiences of school-aged children with thalassemia and the roles of caregivers and nurses in supporting adherence to treatment plans. Thirty key informants, comprising 12 school-aged children with thalassemia, 10 primary caregivers, and eight nurses, were purposively selected from a secondary-level hospital in Thailand. Research instruments included a demographic data form and a semi-structured in-depth interview guide. Content validity was assessed by three experts, with content validity index values ranging from .67 to 1.00. Data were collected through in-depth interviews. Demographic data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, while qualitative data were analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings revealed four main themes concerning the children’s self-management experiences: 1) disease awareness and understanding, which varied across three levels according to age and developmental stage; 2) self-care behaviors related to medication taking, dietary control, and symptom management; 3) barriers and challenges, including fear of blood draws, cravings for restricted foods, and feelings of being different from peers; and 4) motivation and supportive factors, including family support and intrinsic motivation. Caregiver roles encompassed five dimensions: nutritional management, medication management, emotional support, care coordination, and coping with caregiving burdens. Nursing roles encompassed four areas: clinical assessment and monitoring, education, psychosocial support, and care coordination.

items.title: “It Felt Like Practicing Telemedicine While Learning About It”: A Reflexive Thematic Analysis of Medical Students’ Reflective Diaries from a Telemedicine Elective Course Across two Cohorts
items.abstract: Abstract Background Telemedicine has shifted from a niche modality to an established component of routine clinical practice in many health systems. Medical curricula are only beginning to address this shift. Reflective writing is increasingly used both as a pedagogical tool in medical education and as a data source for qualitative research on student attitudes. The experiences and conceptual journeys of pre-clinical medical students enrolled in dedicated telemedicine instruction are under-studied, particularly across multiple cohorts spanning the COVID-19 and post-pandemic periods. Methods We conducted a reflexive thematic analysis of 81 reflective diaries written by students (predominantly second-year medical students) enrolled in an elective telemedicine course at a single Israeli medical school across two cohorts distinguished by consent procedure: a retrospective cohort (2019–2024, n = 39), in which students who had already submitted diaries as a routine course component were contacted by email in 2025 (after ethical approval was granted) and asked to consent retrospectively to use of their diaries in research; and a prospective cohort (2025, n = 42), in which students were informed at the start of the course that the diaries would be analyzed and were asked to enclose a signed consent form with the diary they submitted. Analysis followed Braun and Clarke’s six-phase reflexive thematic analytic framework with an inductive orientation. Results Six overarching themes were identified: (1) a transformative conceptual journey from skepticism or naïveté to conviction; (2) telemedicine as the inevitable trajectory of medicine and a site of professional-identity formation; (3) recognition of telemedicine as a holistic discipline drawing on multiple lenses; (4) a productive tension between equity gains and erosion of the doctor–patient bond; (5) lived experience (as patient, family member, or in prior professional roles) functioning as an explicit interpretive lens; and (6) pedagogy and the medium of delivery, with the Zoom format read by students as enacting the course’s argument. The thematic structure was stable across cohorts. Distributional shifts in the prospective (2025) cohort included articulation of artificial-intelligence displacement concerns, focused engagement with breaking-bad-news as a boundary case, named concerns about defensive prescribing, the war (October 2023 onward) as a catalyzing event alongside COVID-19, increased advocacy for converting the course from an elective to a curricular requirement, and emerging attention to online patient and clinician communities as a distinct dimension of digital medicine. Conclusions This multi-cohort qualitative analysis identifies six stable themes and documents strong, consistent positive engagement with a pre-clinical telemedicine elective across both cohorts. Students describe the course as a formative and highly valuable learning experience, engage substantively with the multi-dimensional character of telemedicine, and read the Zoom delivery format as enacting the course’s content — an effect we describe as pedagogical resonance. Differences in the articulation of certain sub-themes (notably AI-displacement concerns and humanistic boundary cases such as breaking bad news) were more prominent in the prospective (2025) cohort and reflect the evolving discourse on digital medicine; these are cross-sectional differences and do not warrant longitudinal or causal inference. Taken together, our findings make a strong case for the inclusion of dedicated telemedicine instruction as a core component of the pre-clinical medical curriculum.

items.title: “NEW HUMANISM” AS A FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLE IN THE WORKS WRITTEN BY K. ISHIGURO AND Y. TAWADA
items.abstract: The article conceptualizes the artistic dimensions of “new humanism” in transcultural prose, based on K. Ishiguro’s novels “Never Let Me Go”, “Klara and the Sun” and Y. Tawada’s “Suspicious Characters on a Night Train”. It is suggested that rapid technological progress, the emergence of artificial intelligence, and the crisis of traditional humanistic values manifested in the studied works require a re-evaluation of the human essence in the era of metamodernism. The sense of alienation and the inability to become a part of any community make it possible to examine the literary works through the lens of the postcolonial theories. Thus, the article also analyzes the transition from postmodern irony to metamodernist “new sincerity” under the conditions of technological progress. The poetics of representing this new identity and the transformation of the “self-other” dichotomy are investigated through the material of contemporary British and Japanese literature. It is established that despite the challenges of digitalization, basic ethical guidelines remain the foundation of humanistic values in any era, particularly in times of severe social challenges. Universal categories such as empathy, love, kindness, tolerance, respect for biological differences, and the ability to bear responsibility for one’s own inventions and actions acquire particular significance. As a result of the study, it has been proven that the writers gradually abandon postmodern irony and nihilism, turning to the so-called “cautious optimism”. It has been substantiated that K. Ishiguro and Y. Tawada overcome cultural dislocation by creating a special third, intermediate space where a world-open personality is formed.

items.title: “Time and Position”, Cosmic Principle, and Delights in Heaven: Examining the View of Shengsi 生死 (Life and Death) in the Study of Yijing
items.abstract: The problem of shengsi 生死 (life and death) is one of the most fundamental and intractable questions of human existence, yet remarkably little systematic work has been done on the Yijing’s own conception of sheng 生 (life) and si 死 (death) as an integrated philosophical and religious problem. Drawing on the Yijing text, the later commentaries, and conceptual analysis, this study seeks to fill this gap by investigating the Yijing’s conception of sheng 生 (life) and si 死 (death) in its three basic structural perspectives: “time and position” (shi wei 時位), the cosmological alternation of yin and yang, and the existential posture of “delighting in Heaven” (le tian 樂天). The first perspective shows that sheng 生 (life) and si 死 (death) are situational states depending on one’s circumstance within changing configurations of time and position. The second perspective lifts this situational awareness to the level of cosmic principle: sheng 生 (life) being the union of yin and yang, si 死 (death) as their separation, both of which are necessary phases in the endless process of cosmic generation. The third perspective traces the process by which this cosmological understanding was internalized. It leads to an existential attitude of “delights in Heaven and knows his own fate and what Heaven bestows” (le tian zhi ming 樂天知命), a condition in which the fear of si 死 (death) is overcome by acceptance. In this case, the meaning of sheng 生 (life) and si 死 (death) is fulfilled in the realization and accomplishment of one’s “will” (zhi 志) and “nature” (xing 性) endowed by Heaven. The study concludes that the Yijing offers a philosophical and religious vision in which sheng 生 (life) and si 死 (death) are not opposed and separated, but integrated as complementary phases of a single, ongoing process of cosmic and human realization. It speaks to the perennial human question of how finite beings, conscious of their mortality, can find meaning and fulfilment in a world of constant change.

items.title: $τ$-Emotion-Bench: Exposing the Interaction Fragility of LLM Agents through Real-World User Emotions
items.abstract: In long-horizon tool-calling tasks, LLM agents can fail not only because of tool-use errors, but also because of ineffective interaction with users. Yet existing benchmarks largely assume cooperative and behaviorally stable users, leaving the effect of emotional variation on agent reliability underexplored. We introduce $τ$-Emotion-Bench, a ten-domain benchmark for evaluating tool-calling agents under controlled emotion-conditioned user interactions while preserving the underlying task objective. To scale both benchmark construction and agent training, we introduce Tracer, a scalable agentic data-generation pipeline that constructs grounded, policy-valid tasks and collects trajectories through an interactive agent--user--environment harness. By allowing dissatisfied users to terminate inefficient interactions, the harness provides an interaction-aware signal that filters trajectories with excessive user dependence and favors effective tool use. Experiments with two user simulators show that frontier agents remain unreliable, with substantial gaps between average task success and consistent task completion. Tracer-generated supervision consistently improves Qwen3 models across scales, generalizes to unseen domains, and transfers to $τ$-Bench and $τ$-Trait. Behavioral analyses further show that higher task success is associated with a better balance between tool execution and necessary user follow-up. Overall, $τ$-Emotion-Bench and Tracer provide a scalable framework for evaluating agent reliability under diverse user behaviors and improving tool-calling agents through interaction-aware supervision.

items.title: 3D Digital Modeling Empowering Sculpture Education
items.abstract: This paper explores the application of 3D modeling software in sculpture education and proposes a data-driven framework called “Adaptive Sculpture-3D,” aimed at addressing the lack of real-time feedback and the challenges of cognitive load management in traditional teaching. Through case analysis and quantitative experiments, the study validates the effectiveness of the framework in improving students' creation accuracy (with a 21.8% reduction in vertex error rate) and self-efficacy (medium effect size of 0.74), while also revealing limitations in enhancing operational efficiency (effect size of 0.38). The experimental results demonstrate that the real-time feedback mechanism of the framework significantly optimizes the learning process, though caution is needed to avoid learner dependency caused by excessive prompts. This research provides empirical support for the digital curriculum design in art institutions and envisions future developments integrating generative artificial intelligence and multimodal data.

items.title: 44th National Congress of the Italian Society of Nephrology Nurses (SIAN)
items.abstract: The 44th National Congress of the Italian Society of Nephrology Nurses (SIAN), held in Bologna, Italy, from 4 to 6 May 2026, provided a national forum for discussion on the evolving role of nursing in nephrology. The Congress was preceded by a dedicated pre-congress session focused on education, research, and clinical practice, with particular attention to the involvement of nursing students and early-career professionals in scientific activities. Across plenary sessions, round tables, workshops, oral communications, and digital poster presentations, the scientific programme addressed major areas of contemporary nephrology nursing, including professional development, patient-centred care, vascular access management, dialysis technologies, kidney transplantation, symptom management, home and community care, digital health, artificial intelligence, sustainability, and nutritional care. Particular attention was given to the integration of evidence-based practice, clinical expertise, technological innovation, interprofessional collaboration, and patient education. This Conference Proceedings provides an overview of the scientific and educational activities of the meeting and brings together the accepted contributions presented during both the pre-congress session and the main Congress. Collectively, these contributions illustrate the diversity and continued development of nephrology nursing practice and research in Italy and highlight the importance of scientific societies in promoting professional competence, knowledge exchange, and innovation in kidney care.

items.title: A de-identified inpatient clinical pathway dataset integrating ICD-10 diagnoses, ICD-9-CM procedures, Indonesian Case-Based Groups (INA-CBG), and length of stay for healthcare analytics
items.abstract: Background Healthcare administrative databases have become indispensable resources for healthcare analytics, hospital management, clinical pathway analysis, health services research and artificial intelligence. Modern hospital information systems routinely collect standardized diagnoses, procedures, reimbursement classifications, and hospitalization outcomes in everyday clinical practice. Despite their importance, publicly accessible datasets integrating diagnosis codes, procedure codes, case-mix classifications, and hospitalization outcomes remain scarce, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). The absence of comprehensive administrative datasets limits reproducible research in clinical pathway modelling, healthcare operations, reimbursement analysis, and machine learning. To address this gap, we developed and publicly released a de-identified inpatient clinical pathway dataset derived from routine hospital administrative records processed through the Indonesian Case-Based Groups (INA-CBG) reimbursement system. Methods The dataset was constructed from finalized inpatient hospitalization records collected between November 2016 and April 2026. Clinical diagnoses were represented using the International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10), and clinical procedures were encoded using the International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-9-CM). Each hospitalization episode included one primary diagnosis, up to 11 secondary diagnoses, one primary procedure, up to 16 secondary procedures, one INA-CBG classification code, one INA-CBG description, and one length-of-stay (LOS) variable. Data extraction, transformation, harmonization, de-identification, quality assessment, and validation were performed using a reproducible Python-based computational workflow. The final repository contained 165,391 hospitalization episodes represented by 32 standardized variables. Conclusions The dataset provides an openly available resource for healthcare analytics, clinical pathway research, process mining, hospital management, reimbursement analysis, predictive modelling, explainable artificial intelligence, and healthcare operational research. The combination of standardized ICD-10 diagnoses, ICD-9-CM procedures, INA-CBG classifications, and hospitalization outcomes enables diverse secondary analyses while maintaining interoperability with existing healthcare information systems. All datasets, metadata, source codes, and supporting documentation are publicly available through Zenodo to facilitate transparency, reproducibility, and future methodological development.

items.title: A digital leadership cycle for strengthening primary teachers’ lesson planning
items.abstract: Background—Primary teachers need support to translate digital access into pedagogically coherent lesson plans and teaching materials. Objectives—This study examined five connected aspects of principals’ support: diagnosing digital-learning needs, enabling situated professional learning, orchestrating digital resources, evaluating practice and renewing support, and synthesizing a cross-case leadership cycle. Method—A qualitative multiple-case study was conducted in four public primary schools in Muaro Jambi, Indonesia. Four principals and eight experienced upper-primary teachers participated, providing accounts complemented by non-participant observations and school documents. Within-case summaries and cross-case matrices were interpreted through source and method triangulation and member checking. Results—The cases shared needs diagnosis, workplace learning, resource coordination, and formative supervision, but differed in the evidence used, learning arrangements, and access constraints. Teaching materials considered in the study included teaching modules, worksheets, digital media, and assessments; no standardized improvement scores were available. Education-report analysis was prominent in Case A and Case B, peer-supported learning in Case C, and phase-based discussion in Case D. The synthesis yielded a diagnose–enable–evaluate–renew cycle, with resource orchestration embedded in enablement. Conclusions—The cycle offers a context-sensitive explanation of leadership support for digital lesson planning. It is an interpretive proposition for further testing, rather than evidence of causal effects on teacher competence or student outcomes.

items.title: A Dual-Loop Intelligent Teaching Assistant System for Adaptive Web-Based Teaching and Decision Support
items.abstract: Web-based technologies often fail to fundamentally reshape teaching processes, despite their ubiquity. This study presents a dual-loop intelligent teaching assistant system that integrates natural language processing-driven intent recognition and sentiment analysis within a human-in-the-loop framework. Unlike systems prioritizing pure automation, this study's architecture dynamically routes complex queries to instructors via a visual decision-support dashboard, balancing real-time responsiveness with pedagogical nuance. Empirical results in higher education reveal that while interaction efficiency improved significantly, user satisfaction depended nonlinearly on technical accuracy, heavily influenced by notification strategies and emergent student behaviors, like reverse engineering the bot. These findings underscore the need to evolve web-based tools from static utilities into adaptive sociotechnical ecosystems that actively support both learner autonomy and instructor decision-making.

items.title: A Dual-Stage Vision–Language Framework for Dental Report Generation
items.abstract: Panoramic dental radiographs are routinely used for diagnosis and treatment planning, yet their interpretation remains time-consuming and highly dependent on clinical expertise. Although Vision–Language Models (VLMs) have shown promising capabilities for medical report generation, their application to dental radiology is constrained by the scarcity of expert-written report datasets and the computational cost of domain-specific fine-tuning. This paper proposes a dual-stage framework for automated report generation from panoramic dental radiographs that integrates structured visual analysis with pretrained VLMs. In the first stage, dedicated deep learning models extract clinically relevant information through tooth detection with FDI numbering, dental pathology detection, and tooth segmentation. Specifically, two YOLO-based models perform tooth localization and pathology detection, while a U-Net-ResNet34 segmentation model generates tooth masks for constructing contour-based region-of-interest images. In the second stage, these findings are organized into a structured representation that guides pretrained VLMs through prompting. The vision models achieved an mAP at 0.50 of 0.95 for tooth detection and 0.60 for pathology detection, and 94.6% of the detected lesions were assigned to the correct tooth. Five open-weight VLMs were evaluated under four input configurations with an LLM-as-a-Judge, and the best-performing model, Qwen2.5-VL-3B, was further assessed by dental experts on 100 radiographs from an independent external dataset. Incorporating the structured findings increased the proportion of clinically relevant reports from 1.5% to 80.0–81.5%, achieved a pathology precision of up to 76.0%, and reduced the hallucination rate from 53.7% to 14.0–16.8%. These results show that structured visual findings enable small pretrained VLMs to generate clinically relevant dental reports without large-scale image–report datasets or VLM fine-tuning.

items.title: A Flexible Cognitive Built Wearable Platform Using Multimodal Therapeutic Sensors and Reinforcement Learning Technique for Upper-Limb Stroke Rehabilitation
items.abstract: Stroke is one of the most common long-term motor disabilities which requires a personalized rehabilitation strategy capable of delivering reliable therapeutic interventions with continuous assessment. This paper proposes the integration of the inertial measurement unit, force-sensing technology, and electromyography (EMG), along with an artificial intelligence (AI)-based, cognitive–adaptive control platform and intelligent framework within a closed loop for precision neurorehabilitation. This research proposes a methodology to continuously monitor patients’ motor functions and compensate for movements, dynamically optimize rehabilitation, and detect fatigue intensity in real time. This proposed architecture combines deep learning-based movement analysis with multimodal sensor fusion and reinforcement learning-based adaptive control. This is done alongside cloud-based facility analytics for long-term longitudinal assessment and clinic medical assistant therapy management, and a lightweight edge computing module for feature extraction and cognitive decision-making. A total of 36 post-stroke patients with upper-limb hemiplegia were used in an 8-week clinical study, in which Fugl–Meyer assessment (FMA) scores increased by an average of 87.9%, EMG muscle activation by 42.8%, and therapy efficiency improved by 31.6%. Therapy efficiency improved by 32.8% and 21.9% rehabilitation reduction when compared with traditional physiotherapy. The composite performance index has rapidly increased to 0.949, indicating overall rehabilitation efficiency, with repeated measures analysis of variance confirming a statistically significant trend. Thus, the home-based stroke recovery with substantial potential for research constrains the healthcare environment with smart adaptive and real-time patient-specific optimization, which is proposed in this AI framework as an interpretable clinical deployment solution.

items.title: A framework for safe, ethical, and trustworthy AI deployment and integration in hospitals: a systematic review and regulatory gap analysis with emphasis on the U.S. regulatory context
items.abstract: Background The rapid deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) in U.S. hospitals has outpaced regulatory frameworks. By end-2025, the FDA had authorized over 1,451 AI-enabled medical devices, yet governance remains fragmented and reactive. Although the regulatory analysis focuses on the United States, the review included international evidence where directly relevant to U.S. hospital governance, and U.S.-specific conclusions rest primarily on the U.S.-based evidence. Objectives This systematic review and regulatory gap analysis examined the current state of AI governance in U.S. hospitals, identified critical gaps between existing regulations and governance needs, and proposed a comprehensive framework for safe and trustworthy AI deployment. Methods The review was conducted and reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Four databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar) were searched for peer-reviewed articles published from January 2017 through January 2026 (final searches 15–18 January 2026). The PICOS framework structured inclusion criteria. Quality was assessed using CASP, NOS, and QUADAS-2 according to study design. A narrative synthesis approach was employed, followed by a structured regulatory gap analysis of federal statutes, regulations, and agency guidance. Results Of 1,065 records identified, 22 studies met the eligibility criteria. In the systematic review, FDA, ONC, and CMS standards were inconsistent and poorly tailored to AI's evolving capabilities, with evidence of inconsistency between pre-market approval and real-world performance, underutilization of continuous surveillance, and failure to conduct subgroup bias analyses. The regulatory gap analysis identified four critical gaps: post-market surveillance deficiencies, equity protection failures, accountability clarification shortcomings, and governance capacity disparities. Interpretation of these findings for U.S. regulatory policy is provided separately in the regulatory gap analysis and the Discussion. Conclusion A lifecycle governance framework is needed, incorporating continuous monitoring, transparency assurance, equity safeguards, accountability mechanisms, and scalable governance structures to ensure safe, ethical, and trustworthy AI deployment in healthcare. Key limitations include the retrospective protocol registration, the restriction to English-language publications, and the heterogeneity of the included evidence.
