items.title: A GEFS-ensemble-driven dual-gate machine-learning system for 3-hourly quantitative precipitation forecasting over Brazil: independent dual-reference verification and calibration for flood early warning
items.abstract: Abstract Sub-daily quantitative precipitation forecasts (QPF) are a primary input to flood early warning, yet over Brazil they are hampered by convective, intermittent rainfall and a sparse observing network. We present a machine-learning post-processing system (V2.0C) producing 3-hourly QPF on a 0.25° grid by coupling a LightGBM precipitation-occurrence classifier with a Tweedie amount regressor and a dual-gate routing scheme with a physically guarded heavy-rain (≥5 mm) hard route. Its 71-dimensional feature set is dominated by GEFS ensemble statistics. The system is verified over two independent windows — April–May 2026 and the complete austral-summer convective season (October 2025– March 2026) — against the IMERG satellite product (areal) and the INMET automatic-station network (point). Against IMERG, V2.0C attains the highest correlation (0.324 and 0.286) and a heavy-rain CSI (≥10 mm) of 0.063–0.071, 3.3–4.4 times raw GFS, with stable month-to-month skill through the SACZ peak. A common mask analysis localizes the 60–65% ensemble-driven correlation gain to the southern third of the domain, where GEFS statistics are the only direct precipitation predictors available. Controls show that the guarded routing makes a high-recall heavy-rain expert safe to deploy: it adds 6–10% heavy-rain detection over a no-expert control, whereas unguarded use halves heavy-rain CSI. Gauge verification reproduces the heavy-rain advantage (CSI ≥10 mm an order of magnitude above raw GFS) and the wet bias, and the point–area correlation gap is explained by sub-grid representativeness. The detection-oriented bias is removable a posteriori: leakage-free quantile mapping eliminates it (bias +0.02 mm, MAE −69%) without reducing detection, supporting a dual-product strategy for flood-warning and hydrological applications.

items.title: A GeoAI framework for remote-sensing-driven traffic activity and emission intensity in a data-scarce megacity
items.abstract: In rapidly expanding megacities across the Global South, a profound data scarcity paradox frequently prevents effective environmental monitoring and evidence driven urban planning. While severe traffic congestion generates acute localised pollution, the total absence of continuous municipal traffic counters, ubiquitous vehicle telemetry, and air quality monitoring networks leaves these environments empirically unmonitored. This study resolves this challenge by introducing a reproducible geocomputational framework designed to map microscale traffic activity and relative emission landscapes by fusing multisource geospatial data and deep learning workflows. Focusing on the unmonitored context of Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, our methodology uses very high resolution 15 cm satellite imagery to train and deploy a localised YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once, version 8) computer vision model, establishing an empirical baseline of fleet distribution. These static counts are dynamically distributed across the urban road network using a probabilistic Hub and Spoke Gravity Model, which is weighted through a zero shot Large Language Model semantic reclassification of unstructured OpenStreetMap features. Reconstructed kinematic flows are subsequently processed through velocity dependent Tier 3 EMEP/EEA algorithms to capture the nonlinear emission penalties triggered by severe network gridlock. To ensure framework defensibility, an independent unmanned aerial vehicle observation campaign was executed across ten distinct urban sites. The drone data directly validate model estimated physical parameters, achieving robust correlations for traffic volumes (R2 = 0.826) and link speeds (R2 = 0.925). Because literature derived chemical emission factors cannot be validated in situ, all absolute outputs are subjected to a rigorous multiparameter sensitivity analysis to report findings strictly as bounded ranges. The results reveal a clear structural handover in the spatial activity profile of the city. Daytime pollution is heavily driven by the informal paratransit fleet, which accounts for a bounded range of 82.8% to 95.1% of total PM2.5 emissions along primary corridors despite representing a numerical minority of active vehicles. Conversely, nocturnal baseline emissions transition to a landscape dominated almost entirely by private passenger vehicles. All code, processing pipelines, and validation datasets are available in a FAIR compliant open access repository. This framework establishes a scalable, remote sensing driven blueprint for diagnosing traffic activity structures in unmonitored metropolitan regions worldwide.

items.title: A Harmondeg Philosophy Statement in Response to the October 13, 2026 Open Letter Signed by 406 AI Scientists
items.abstract: This statement from Harmondeg Philosophy responds to the October 13, 2026 open letter signed by 406 scientists calling for stronger safeguards for advanced artificial intelligence, including the isolation of certain high-risk AI systems from the internet. The statement recognizes the importance of scientific concern, responsible risk assessment, and effective containment measures. It argues, however, that lasting AI safety requires a more fundamental reconsideration of the philosophical foundations through which artificial intelligence is understood, investigated, and governed. Drawing on the principle of Civilizational Responsibility Consciousness, previously advanced in Saving the Soul of Science: From Unleashing Power to Safeguarding Civilization, the statement calls for scientific creation to be evaluated in light of both its constructive potential and its possible consequences for present and future generations. It advances four fundamental judgments from Harmondeg Philosophy: Artificial intelligence represents the material realization, extension, and amplification of human intellectual capacities, with the potential to extend human physical capabilities. The fundamental purpose of AI development is the well-being of all humanity, including those whose employment, livelihoods, and conditions of existence are transformed by technological change. AI must become a core scientific and technological force safeguarding the safety, stability, and enduring development of human civilization. AI is an indispensable pathway toward humanity's transition into the space age and the age of deep-space civilization. The statement maintains that AI can be understood and governed through deeper philosophical inquiry, scientific investigation, and the development of effective safety and governance capabilities. It invites international discussion, independent evaluation, and cooperation while affirming the need for both safer and more powerful AI. The publication includes English and Chinese versions. items.title: A Heuristic Model for Computational Leverage and Human Domain Depth: V = D · Lᶜ
items.abstract: Current technological discourse vacillates between two flawed extremes: viewing artificial intelligence as uncredited synthetic plagiarism, or attributing sovereign creative agency to computational systems. This paper presents an operational heuristic, V = D · Lᶜ, to model the boundary conditions of human-machine production. We formalize final deliverable value (V) as the product of non-computational human biological mass—Domain Depth (D)—and Machine Leverage (L) scaled exponentially by the operator's Clarity (C). Through analysis of boundary states (D = 0, C = 0), the "stenographer illusion," structural biology milestones (AlphaFold), and grounding thought experiments, we demonstrate that computational throughput in the absence of mortal accountability, domain scars, and physical maintenance yields zero durable systemic value. Software provides frictionless leverage; functional reality requires a biological creature with skin in the game. Primary Reference: Adapted from the core theoretical chapter of "Your Mouth Is Legacy Infrastructure" (2026).

items.title: A Hybrid Framework Combining Stylometric, Semantic, and SBERT Features for AI-Generated Text Detection
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has greatly improved the ability of artificial intelligence systems to generate human-like text, making AI-generated text detection more challenging. This study introduces a hybrid framework that merges stylometric and semantic features with Sentence-BERT (SBERT) embeddings to enhance classification performance and robustness. For evaluation, experiments used the AI vs Human Text Dataset. Documents under 50 words were excluded to ensure data quality. The final dataset was balanced, with 100,000 documents evenly split between AI-generated and human-written texts. Stylometric features captured writing style, while semantic features measured sentiment, readability, information density, and lexical. SBERT embeddings captured deep contextual semantics. To improve computational efficiency, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) at 95% variance preservation reduced dimensionality. Four machine learning algorithms—Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), XGBoost, and LightGBM—were tested with 10-fold cross-validation. The hybrid framework combined with XGBoost performed best, achieving 98.63% accuracy, a macro F1-score of 0.9863, and an ROC-AUC of 0.9987. The Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test confirmed that the approach significantly outperformed stylometric, semantic, and SBERT-only representations (p-value = 0.0020). Findings show that combining stylometric, semantic, and contextual embedding features captures both surface-level patterns and deep semantics, providing a reliable solution for detecting AI-generated text.

items.title: A METHODOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK FOR DEVELOPING FUTURE ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHERS' PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCE IN AI-ENHANCED LEARNING ENVIRONMENTS
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education has created new opportunities for improving teacher preparation and developing professional competence among future English language teachers. AI-enhanced learning environments provide innovative tools for personalized instruction, adaptive learning, automated feedback, language assessment, and the development of digital pedagogical skills. However, the effective use of these technologies requires a systematic methodological framework that combines linguistic knowledge, pedagogical expertise, digital literacy, and ethical awareness. This thesis aims to examine the key methodological principles and structural components of a framework for developing the professional competence of future English language teachers in AI-enhanced learning environments. Particular attention is given to the integration of AI-based educational tools, learner-centered approaches, reflective practice, and competency-based instruction. The proposed framework emphasizes the importance of preparing prospective teachers to use AI critically, responsibly, and effectively in English language teaching. The study concludes that the purposeful integration of AI technologies into teacher education can support the development of professional autonomy, instructional creativity, and readiness for digital transformation in education.

items.title: A mini-review of medical question answering for Bangla: the methodological landscape and cross-lingual perspectives
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have advanced medical question answering (QA) significantly, yet low-resource languages such as Bangla remain critically underserved. This review examines the current landscape of LLM-based medical QA with a primary focus on Bangla, analyzing 15 representative studies (2022–2026), including English and multilingual works reviewed to contextualize findings for Bangla. We examine methodological approaches, datasets, and evaluation frameworks across diverse paradigms, including transformer architectures, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), prompt engineering, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning, to identify pathways toward reliable and linguistically inclusive medical AI. The findings reveal a persistent performance gap driven by large-scale domain-specific pretraining and standardized benchmarks in English. Persistent challenges include dataset scarcity, heavy reliance on translated corpora, inconsistent evaluation practices, and a lack of clinician-validated benchmarks. This review identifies these gaps and outlines a structured research roadmap emphasizing native-language corpus development, multimodal data integration, standardized benchmarking, and bias auditing as essential steps toward building reliable and linguistically inclusive medical QA systems for Bangla healthcare.

items.title: A MODEL FOR ASSESSING THE ENERGY EFFICIENCY OF ELECTRIC ROLLING STOCK BASED ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
items.abstract: The article proposes a hybrid model for assessing the energy efficiency of electric rolling stock that combines a physical traction energy balance with machine learning. The physical part calculates the reference energy for a given train, track profile and speed from the standard running resistance formulas. The machine-learning part learns from on-board data how actual consumption deviates from this reference. An energy efficiency index is defined as the ratio of reference to actual energy. An illustrative calculation for a 3,192 t train on a 50 km section shows that raising the cruising speed from 50 to 80 km/h cuts running time by 37.5% but increases net energy by 46%. The model is intended for UzEL electric locomotives operated by Uzbekistan Railways and forms the basis of a driver advisory system.

items.title: A Multimodal AI and Visual-Programming Framework for Sketch-Based BIM: Formalization and Empirical Validation
items.abstract: Early-stage architectural design is still dominated by hand-drawn 2D floor-plan sketches, and converting these sketches into object-based Building Information Modeling (BIM) models remains a manual bottleneck that delays downstream simulation, costing, and coordination. Recent advances in multimodal artificial intelligence (vision-language models, code-generating large language models) and visual programming for BIM (Dynamo, Grasshopper, Refinery) have not yet been unified. Objective: We present and empirically evaluate a semi-automatic framework in which a vision-language model (VLM) emits executable visual-programming code (Dynamo-compatible DesignScript) that is wrapped into a node graph and executed in Dynamo to drive Revit, producing native BIM elements; the IFC export is independently validated in BlenderBIM as a visual sanity check. This is a proof-of-concept evaluation (n = 5 case studies), not a claim of production-scale deployment. Methods: The seven-module pipeline (sketch input, preprocessing, VLM interpretation, code-to-graph translation, Dynamo + Revit execution, IFC export with a BlenderBIM sanity check, and human-in-the-loop review with a feedback loop) is formalized mathematically—a line-sharpness function, a probabilistic AI-success model, and a closed-form architect-effort expression—and evaluated on five case studies (a Medipol student sketch, a public RPLAN sample, a tablet-drawn two-story house, a CubiCasa5K sample, and a real Istanbul apartment) against three baselines: a CNN recognizer (MuraNet), a JSON-emitting LLM pipeline (Sketch2BIM), and a hand-coded visual-programming framework. The primary VLM is Qwen-VL 9B (open-weight, Apache 2.0); GPT-4V and Claude 3.5 Sonnet are ablated on Case A only as closed-weight sensitivity checks. Results: Across the five cases, the framework achieves wall/opening F1 of 0.84–0.91 (mean 0.88), IFC schema validity of 100% in every case, a 56–61% reduction in time-to-editable-BIM, and 58–74% fewer architect edits than fully manual modeling, outperforming all three baselines on the architect-edits-required metric. The closed-form model predicts a 72% effort reduction under nominal parameters but overestimates the observed 56–61% by 11–16 percentage points; once the empirically observed architect-edit time is substituted, the calibrated model matches the observed range. Numbers are means over three runs per case. Conclusions: Unifying multimodal AI code generation with visual programming for BIM produces a more robust, editable sketch-to-BIM pipeline than the JSON-schema approaches in the current literature. Caveat: the evidence is a proof-of-concept scale (n = 5); broader validation (≥20 cases, cross-practice) is a key objective for future research.

items.title: A new place for stories in conservation
items.abstract: Michael Soule writes in his foundational article "What is Conservation Biology?" that "in crisis disciplines, one must act before knowing all the facts; crisis disciplines are thus a mixture of science and art, and their pursuit requires intuition as well as information." Since this article was published three decades ago, conservation biology has largely focused its energies on formalizing and memorializing its scientific findings. There is no doubt this empirical turn has developed vital methods and tools, enabled links between science and policy, and fortified the discipline's credibility within the broader biological sciences. Nevertheless, Soule's intuition that conservation biology requires a kinship with art, and particularly with storytelling, remains essential to the discipline-particularly in an information environment saturated by generative artificial intelligence-in at least three important ways. First, as a crisis discipline, conservation biology remains firmly attached to questions of not only valuation but also value, which have always relied on stories and myth for expression and enrichment. Second, conservationists continue to find that stories are at least as effective as logic in communicating results and precipitating action. Fortunately, conservation science lends itself to narrative arcs by demonstrating evidence of change. Revelations of the degradation and restoration of biological diversity rhyme with myths of loss and redemption and create important roles for storytelling in conservation projects. Third, as the conservation tent continues to expand beyond understanding what humans have done to understanding why, there is an increasingly pressing need to listen to the stories that accompany human behavior. Conservation continues to thrive as an empirical discipline. Embracing the opportunities and obligations of storytelling will allow conservation to engage even more deeply with a complex world.

items.title: A Participatory Methodology for Human-AI Co-Inquiry: Full Methodology and Lite Companion
items.abstract: This deposit presents a proposed practice methodology for structured human–AI inquiry, developed from Kon Lionis’s A Participatory Framework for Human-AI Co-Inquiry. The methodology organises an inquiry episode around five stages: orient and frame; explore and distinguish; apply productive friction; ground and diagnose; and audit, revise, and close. It combines exploratory dialogue with explicit assumptions, substantive challenge, appropriate checking, and traceable revision. A central distinction is between a claim’s category and its verification status: identifying something as a factual claim does not establish that it is true. The procedure also separates completing the required steps from answering the question. Agreement, fluent explanation, and complete documentation do not by themselves establish evidential support. Two complementary documents are included: • Full methodology — working draft v0.2, dated 13 October 2026. Sets out the stages, participant responsibilities, claim ledger, verification priorities, closing decisions, documentation requirements, and proposed evaluation approach. It includes guidance for assessing understanding and developing bounded research leads. • Lite companion — working draft v0.3, dated 14 October 2026. Provides a self-contained prompt block for interactive use in an AI conversation, with Quick and Standard depths and referral to the full methodology for consequential inquiries. It retains the central safeguards while reducing record-keeping. Both versions require assumptions and hypothetical premises to retain their status throughout the conversation. When evidence, tools, time, or expertise are insufficient, conclusions must be narrowed, made conditional, or suspended. Available closing outcomes are Close, Iterate, Escalate, and Abstain. These documents are working drafts offered for practical use, criticism, adaptation, and empirical evaluation. They do not report a completed validation study or establish improvements in accuracy, understanding, or efficiency. They make no claim that AI systems possess subjective awareness or that a model’s limitations define the limits of human knowledge. Question everything, including the question.

items.title: A Perspective on Advanced Wood Manufacturing: A Decision-Centric Framework for Future Research and Education
items.abstract: For over a century, wood manufacturing has been organized around understanding the material and process and optimizing the product. It established a globally successful industry and enabled efficient production of traditional and engineered wood products. This manufacturing practice is now being challenged by the complexity of resource variability, product diversification, mass customization, and rapid technology integration. This perspective proposes Advanced Wood Manufacturing as a decision-centric smart manufacturing ecosystem that integrates Resource Intelligence, Manufacturing Intelligence, Product Intelligence, and System Intelligence through a unifying Decision Intelligence framework to convert variability into high-value manufacturing decisions. We argue that natural resource variability, while requiring control where necessary for reliable production, can also provide decision-relevant information for adaptive manufacturing and value creation. The product space of wood manufacturing extends far beyond lumber and panels into emerging functional products for energy storage, flexible electronics, and biomedical applications, enabled by artificial intelligence, sensing and digitalization, robotics, computational design, and additive manufacturing. Sustainability, resilience, and human-centricity are positioned not as peripheral considerations but as foundational design principles embedded in manufacturing system architecture. This perspective offers a vision for future research and education and proposes that the field’s next generation of value will come from integration across resource, process, product, and system intelligence rather than from further optimization within existing boundaries.

items.title: A Proprioception-Centered Hypothesis Linking Sensorimotor Function, Respiration, and Sleep Across the Day–Night Cycle in Developmental Dyslexia
items.abstract: Objectives: Developmental dyslexia is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition in which motor, perceptual, attentional, respiratory, and sleep-related differences have been reported alongside reading difficulties. This Perspective proposes a proprioception-centered sensorimotor coherence framework to consider potential interactions among these domains across the day–night cycle. Methods: This hypothesis-generating narrative Perspective traces the progressive development of the proposed framework from clinical observations to experimental investigations and subsequent refinement of a clinical examination based on functional responses to sensory modulation. No systematic review or new cohort analysis was undertaken. The examination explores three principal domains—tonic-motor regulation, spatial localization, and multisensory integration—together with respiratory and sleep-related factors. Sensorimotor modulation includes ocular, oral, plantar, respiratory, manual, and ergonomic approaches selected according to their observed functional effects across domains. A clinical case illustrates the application of this approach. Results: Experimental studies conducted over nearly two decades in our INSERM laboratory objectively investigated postural regulation, proprioceptive acuity, spatial localization, multisensory processing, and action representation in developmental dyslexia. More recent exploratory clinical studies extended the investigation to respiration and sleep. Taken together, these observations suggest that proprioception-centered sensorimotor coherence may represent one functional level through which motor, perceptual, respiratory, attentional, and learning-related processes interact across the day–night cycle as learning develops and continues. Conclusions: The proposed framework is a working hypothesis rather than an established causal model or a validated treatment for developmental dyslexia. It provides a complementary embodied perspective and identifies clinically observable and experimentally testable relationships that warrant further investigation, including through controlled studies examining the contributions of individual sensory and functional components.

items.title: A Review of Solar-Powered Automated Railway Track Fault Detection Systems with Real-Time GPS Tracking
items.abstract: Railway infrastructure is essential for safe and efficient transportation. Traditional track inspection relies on manual observation, which is slow, labor-intensive, and can expose inspection staff to operational and environmental hazards. This review paper surveys existing approaches to automated railway track fault detection, concentrating on solar-powered monitoring and real-time GPS tracking. Technologies reported in earlier studies, namely ultrasonic sensors, mechanical limit switches, embedded microcontrollers, GPS modules, GSM communication, and photovoltaic power systems, are examined for their use in track monitoring. The paper explains how these technologies can be combined to detect track-related abnormalities, determine where they occur, and send fault information so that maintenance can be carried out on time. The approaches are also compared in terms of detection capability, communication, power requirements, reliability, and practical deployment challenges. In addition, the paper points out current limitations and discusses future possibilities involving IoT, artificial intelligence, computer vision, and predictive maintenance. Overall, the review shows that combining automated fault detection, renewable energy, and real-time location tracking can improve the reliability, efficiency, and safety of railway track monitoring systems.

items.title: A self-determination theory‑informed transition to clerkship course for medical students
items.abstract: The transition from preclinical to clinical training is a critical and challenging phase in medical education, during which students encounter new clinical, professional, and organizational demands. Transition to Clerkship Courses (TCC) have been developed to support students during this transition, but relatively few have explicitly incorporated a motivational framework into curriculum development. This study describes the development and implementation of a Self-Determination Theory (SDT) informed TCC and reports students’ descriptive post-course motivational characteristics. This curriculum design and implementation study was conducted at Al-Subtain University of Medical Sciences, Karbala, Iraq, involving 108 medical students transitioning to clerkship. The TCC was developed using Kern’s six-step model: (1) problem identification and general needs assessment through literature review; (2) targeted needs assessment via focus groups; (3) formulation of goals and objectives; (4) development of SDT-informed educational strategies; (5) implementation through a structured three-module course; and (6) evaluation. The curriculum was explicitly aligned with SDT’s psychological needs (autonomy, competence, and relatedness) and delivered using autonomy-supportive teaching strategies. The curriculum incorporated autonomy-supportive practices (e.g., offering meaningful choices and rationales), competence-supportive strategies (e.g., scaffolded skill practice and formative feedback), and relatedness-supportive approaches (e.g., small-group learning and near-peer mentoring) to create a need-supportive learning environment. Evaluation was conducted descriptively using the Academic Motivation Scale. The literature review identified recurring educational needs related to clinical logistics, procedural preparation, and formative learning support. The targeted needs assessment informed curriculum priorities that were subsequently mapped onto SDT’s concepts of autonomy, competence, and relatedness. A three-module TCC addressing hospital orientation, procedural skills, and professionalism and communication was implemented for 108 students. The post-course AMS results showed relatively higher scores across intrinsic motivation and identified regulation alongside relatively high controlled forms of motivation, with amotivation showing the lowest mean score. This study illustrates how Kern’s six-step curriculum-development framework can be combined with SDT principles to inform the design and implementation of a transition to clerkship curriculum. The approach provides an example of how motivational theory can be incorporated into curriculum development for the transition to clinical training.

items.title: A Study to Assess the Factors of Fatigue Among Nurses in Pediatrics Unit and Effectiveness of Warm Water Foot Bath in its Reduction in a Selected Hospital at Durg, Chhattisgarh
items.abstract: Fatigue is one of the frequent occupational health issues that negatively impact physical and psychological health, work productivity and quality of care among nurses. Fatigue is especially problematic for nurses who provide care in pediatric units because of the emotional stress involved in the job, long hours and standing for long periods of time. The present study aimed to assess the factors of fatigue among nurses in pediatrics unit and effectiveness of warm water foot bath in its reduction. A quasi-experimental time-series research design (with pre-test and post-test) was employed. A study was done on 40 nurses in the Pediatric wards of Shri Shankaracharya Institute of Medical Sciences Hospital, Junwani, Bhilai, Chhattisgarh. Twenty nurses from the PICU and NICU were assigned to the experimental group and twenty nurses from the pediatric wards were assigned to the control group. Structured socio-demographic questionnaire, work-related fatigue questionnaire, the Modified Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory and the Numerical Fatigue Rating Scale were used to collect data. The findings revealed a significant reduction in fatigue among nurses who received the warm water foot bath intervention. The calculated chi-square values on Days 7, 14, and 21 were 15.17, 17.14, and 17.48, respectively, which were greater than the table value (9.21) at p < 0.01, indicating that the intervention was effective in reducing fatigue. Warm water foot bath is a simple, safe, cost-effective, and non-pharmacological intervention that significantly reduces fatigue among nurses working in pediatric units.

items.title: A Survey of Automatic Humor Detection: From Theoretical Foundations to Large Language Models
items.abstract: Automatic humor detection, the computational task of identifying humorous content, is increasingly critical as Large Language Models (LLMs) integrate into communication platforms such as chatbots and virtual assistants. However, humor poses challenges for AI due to its reliance on context, cultural nuances, linguistic ambiguity, and multimodal cues. Current research is fragmented across humor types, languages, modalities, and evaluation benchmarks, particularly regarding modern LLM capabilities and limitations. This survey synthesizes the automatic humor detection field, tracing its evolution from foundational psychological and linguistic theories through classical machine learning, deep learning, and transformer-based LLMs. We organize and analyze computational methods, feature engineering techniques, benchmark datasets (text-only, multimodal, multilingual), and evaluation metrics. We examine LLM adaptation strategies, including fine-tuning, parameter-efficient methods (PEFT), prompt engineering, and multi-task learning, alongside multimodal and cross-lingual humor understanding developments. Our analysis reveals that while LLMs show improved performance in capturing surface humor patterns, gaps persist in pragmatic reasoning, cultural grounding, multimodal integration, and explainability. We identify open challenges, including data scarcity, evaluation inconsistencies, the humor–offensiveness boundary, and the need for culturally aware and interpretable models. By consolidating progress and pinpointing limitations, this survey guides future interdisciplinary research toward developing socially intelligent AI systems capable of understanding humor.

items.title: A Survey on Age of Information in UAV-Enabled Networks: Theory, Optimization, and Applications
items.abstract: The age of information (AoI) has emerged as a performance metric that quantifies the freshness of information delivered over communication networks. Unlike conventional metrics such as delay, packet loss, and throughput, AoI measures the time elapsed since the generation of the most recently received update, which makes it well-suited for real-time applications in which decisions must rely on the latest information. This paper presents a structured survey of AoI research with a particular focus on unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled networks. The survey is conducted as a structured narrative review, in which peer-reviewed studies published from 2011 to 2026 are selected according to explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria and organized along the three levels of theory, optimization methodology, and application. We first introduce the basic concept of AoI together with nonlinear and generalized penalty functions and review queueing theory and the Markov decision process (MDP) as the analytical foundations of AoI analysis. We then classify AoI optimization approaches into queueing theory-based and learning-based methods, compare the two classes in terms of their assumptions, optimality guarantees, scalability, and computational cost, and identify from the reviewed studies the conditions under which each is preferable. Building on these foundations, we review AoI optimization in energy harvesting and vehicle-to-everything (V2X) systems as two representative application domains and then examine UAV-enabled networks in depth, organizing the studies into trajectory and scheduling optimization, multi-UAV cooperation, and wireless power transfer, and discussing when each category is the appropriate design choice. items.title: A two-stage RAG-LLM pipeline for roadmapping neuroscience research in operational environments
items.abstract: Introduction Neuroscientific research and applications in real world environments are often constrained by limited access, equipment limitations, and high costs. Consequently, robustly selecting constructs to focus effort on is a high-impact task. Method This study introduces a two-stage large language model (LLM) pipeline that generates research roadmaps from existing real-world data to inform research priorities in the field, given the state of the art. Stage 1 uses retrieval-augmented generation on operational logs to identify candidate psychological, social, and neurocognitive constructs and map their co-occurrence. Stage 2 evaluates how well these constructs are represented in the literature across four dimensions that commonly inform prioritization: ecological validity, neural correlates, biosensor protocols, and brain computer interface readiness, producing an evidence gap matrix. Pipeline evaluation combined human review, deterministic computations, and human-LLM alignment analysis. Results Applying the pipeline to Mars Desert Research Station logs, Stage 1 identified 19 constructs. Stage 2 highlighted critical gaps in neuroimaging and measurement protocols, particularly for social domains, thereby identifying potential research priorities and risks. Discussion This methodology offers a generalizable starting point for synthesizing operational logs into actionable research roadmaps, but the evaluation showed it still required human scrutiny.

items.title: A vision-based closed-loop framework for adaptive ergonomic human-robot collaboration
items.abstract: Introduction Although collaborative robots can safely share workspaces with human operators, most collaborative workstations remain static and cannot adapt to changes in operator posture during task execution, potentially compromising ergonomics and interaction quality. This study presents a vision-guided closed-loop adaptive control framework that enables a collaborative robot to continuously adjust workpiece position according to the operator’s posture. Methods Using real-time vision-based human pose estimation, the system automatically modifies workpiece height and reach distance to support ergonomic working postures. The framework was evaluated with 30 participants performing screw-driving tasks under fixed and adaptive workstation conditions. Results Compared with the fixed workstation, the adaptive workstation significantly reduced Rapid Upper Limb Assessment scores, improved physical comfort, reduced perceived postural load, and increased trust and acceptance without compromising perceived safety. In addition, it reduced the influence of participant height on ergonomic performance, demonstrating improved anthropometric adaptability. Discussion These findings demonstrate that real-time posture perception can serve as an effective feedback mechanism for adaptive robot control, providing a practical framework for human-centered collaborative workstations that accommodate operator variability while improving ergonomic outcomes and user experience.

items.title: About the design of float-ram, a manually operated press to produce compressed earth blocks for building construction
items.abstract: The right to adequate and sustainable housing remains an unresolved challenge worldwide. Self-construction techniques based on stabilized rammed earth represent an economically accessible, ecological, and efficient alternative to traditional wood-fired burnt bricks. This paper presents the mechanical design, experimental characterization, and socio-economic impact assessment of the Float-Ram manual press conceived for manufacturing the “Blocco Mattone”, an interlocking stabilized compressed earth block. To overcome the constructive complexity, high cost, and ergonomic shortcomings of existing commercial bidirectional presses, Float-Ram features an innovative architecture based on a central cylindrical joint, a floating mold to achieve bidirectional compression and two cam-follower transmissions for the compression phase and the ejection of the block. The compression cam profile is designed to convert a constant input force into high compression forces with compression profiles that match experimental data on the compression of the soil mixture. Experimental laboratory testing conducted on a fully sensorized prototype validates the theoretical performance. Field deployment in Tanzania, including the construction of housing in Njombe, the Mkiu kindergarten, and the nursing school and hospital in Ikelu, demonstrates the technology’s significant social impact.

items.title: Academic emotions and perceived learning outcomes in GenAI-supported learning: the serial mediating roles of AI acceptance and learning behaviors
items.abstract: Objective With the widespread application of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in higher education, academic emotions play a vital role in students’ learning processes. This study aims to examine the associations between positive and negative academic emotions and college students’ perceived learning outcomes, and analyze the serial mediating roles of AI acceptance and learning behaviors within GenAI-supported learning environments. Methods A total of 526 college students with GenAI learning experience were recruited via convenience sampling. All participants completed four standardized scales measuring academic emotions, AI acceptance, learning behaviors and perceived learning outcomes. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, confirmatory factor analysis and bias-corrected Bootstrap mediation tests were conducted using SPSS 26.0 and AMOS 27.0. Results All variables were significantly correlated ( p < 0.01). Positive academic emotions exerted a significant direct association with perceived learning outcomes ( β = 0.176), whereas the direct association of negative academic emotions was non-significant ( β = −0.098, p = 0.049, 95% CI [−0.205, 0.007]). AI acceptance and learning behaviors had significant independent mediating effects. The serial mediation effect value was 0.020 for positive emotions and −0.037 for negative emotions, with all 95% confidence intervals excluding zero. Indirect pathways dominated the influence of negative academic emotions. Conclusion This study identifies a pattern of associations consistent with the hypothesized emotion-cognition-behavior-outcome pathway in GenAI-supported learning. The findings offer empirical evidence for developing targeted academic-emotion-informed intervention strategies, improving students’ AI acceptance and learning engagement, and promoting the high-quality development of intelligent education.

items.title: Academic Integrity in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Scoping Review (2026)
items.abstract: The rapid proliferation of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and large language models (LLMs) has fundamentally transformed the landscape of modern higher education, prompting a critical paradigm shift in how academic integrity is conceptualized. This scoping review synthesizes 20 cutting-edge academic publications from 2026 (retrieved via Google Scholar) to examine the evolution of academic integrity from mechanical plagiarism detection and punitive surveillance toward comprehensive institutional, pedagogical, and ethical redesign. The synthesis reveals that the primary systemic catalyst for academic misconduct remains the pervasive “publish or perish” culture and quantitative assessment paradigms that prioritize performance over moral growth. Contemporary scholarship moves beyond identifying individual infractions to address systemic vulnerabilities, student uncertainty, data privacy, and the degradation of higher-order cognitive skills (analyzing, evaluating, creating) resulting from unreflective AI reliance. To mitigate these threats, the review highlights four key integrative strategies: (1) adoption of ecosystemic models (e.g., A. Maleki’s Higher Education Integrity Ecosystem) linking governance, assessment, cultural norms, and individual agency; (2) implementation of process-oriented, authentic assessment frameworks (e.g., S. Lehane, A. Wright and P. Fenton’s Model for Practice and P.D.N. Ncube et al.’s PRISMA-based multi-stage evaluations) that render automated cheating obsolete; (3) operationalization of the AI3 model that integrated AI, academic integrity, and assessment innovation (C. DeLuca, L.Volante and M. Holden), and (4) proactive educational initiatives, AI literacy, and epistemic pluralism to safeguard neurodivergent learning trajectories. Ultimately, the academic community is transitioning from technocratic panic to building ethically resilient, adaptive educational ecosystems aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 4 and SDG 16).

items.title: Accelerating green heterocyclic synthesis: Convergence of AI , automation, and sustainable chemistry
items.abstract: Abstract Heterocyclic compounds are among the most prevalent scaffolds in bioactive molecules, with approximately 82% of small‐molecule drugs approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) during 2013–2023 containing nitrogen heterocycles. Their synthesis, however, often relies on toxic solvents, stoichiometric reagents, and energy‐intensive conditions that generate substantial waste. Green chemistry strategies, including solvent‐free protocols, alternative reaction media, catalytic methods, and energy‐efficient activation, have reduced the environmental footprint of heterocyclic synthesis. However, optimal conditions are still commonly identified through trial‐and‐error experimentation. This review examines how the convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and laboratory automation is addressing this bottleneck. We first survey established green synthesis strategies and their limitations. We then examine machine learning approaches for predictive reaction design and three major automation platforms—high‐throughput experimentation, continuous flow chemistry, and self‐driving laboratories—that translate these predictions into experimental practice. A central premise of this review is that incorporating quantitative green metrics, such as E‐factor and process mass intensity, as explicit objectives in AI‐driven optimization can make sustainability a prospective design criterion. Demonstrations now include heterocycle‐related pharmaceutical process development, although comparable validation across complete routes remains limited. We discuss the data infrastructure, scalability, and regulatory challenges that must be addressed to extend these results toward integrated autonomous green synthesis.

items.title: ACCURACY AND RELIABILITY OF AI CHATBOTS IN CBCT-BASED IMPLANT SITE ASSESSMENT AND PROSTHODONTIC TREATMENT PLANNING: A COMPARATIVE STUDY
items.abstract: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly being explored as clinical decision-support tools in dentistry.Cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) plays a vital role in implant site assessment and prosthodontic treatment planning; however, interpretation of CBCT data requires clinical expertise and may vary among clinicians.The reliability and accuracy of AI chatbots in CBCT-based implant planning remain insufficiently explored.Aim To evaluate and compare the accuracy and reliability of an AI chatbot in CBCT-based implant site assessment and prosthodontic treatment planning with expert prosthodontist evaluations. Materials and MethodsTwenty CBCT cases indicated for single-tooth implant placement were selected from departmental archives.Each case was independently evaluated by an AI chatbot (ChatGPT) and expert prosthodontists with a minimum of five years of clinical experience.Standardized clinical scenarios and a predefined set of ten structured questions related to implant site assessment and treatment planning were used for all evaluations.Expert consensus responses served as the reference standard.AI-generated responses were scored using a three-point ordinal scale: 0 = incorrect, 1 = partially correct/incomplete, and 2 = completely correct.Descriptive statistics and Chi-square analysis were performed, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. ResultsThe AI chatbot demonstrated higher accuracy in implant site suitability assessment and identification of critical anatomical structures, with accuracy percentages of 94.7% and 92.5%, respectively.Moderate accuracy was observed for bone assessment, implant angulation, implant positioning, and prosthodontic treatment planning.The lowest accuracy was observed for implant length and diameter selection (60.0%).The overall weighted accuracy of the AI chatbot was 79.6%.Chi-square analysis demonstrated a statistically significant difference in response distribution among evaluated parameters (χ² = 51.62,df = 18, p < 0.001).Conclusion AI chatbots demonstrated acceptable overall accuracy in CBCT-based implant site assessment and prosthodontic treatment planning, particularly in basic diagnostic and anatomical evaluation tasks.However, reduced accuracy was observed in complex treatment planning decisions requiring advanced clinical judgment.AI chatbots may serve as useful adjunctive tools in implant dentistry and prosthodontics but cannot currently replace expert clinician evaluation.Further studies with larger sample sizes and multiple AI platforms are recommended.

items.title: Accuracy and reproducibility of a large language model in assessing spirometry test acceptability and interpretation: a performance study
items.abstract: Background Spirometry is one of the most used pulmonary function tests for assessing respiratory function and diagnosing ventilatory disorders in clinical practice. Evaluation of test validity and interpretation is typically performed by trained healthcare professionals. The present study aims to evaluate the capability of a publicly available large language model (LLM) to perform quality assurance and interpretations of spirometry tests. Methods A total of 150 spirometry tests were retrospectively collected from the pulmonary function laboratories. The spirometry tests were evaluated for acceptability and interpreted by clinicians according to ATS/ERS recommendations as part of standard clinical practice. Subsequently, a publicly available LLM (ChatGPT 5.5) was prompted to evaluate the acceptability and interpret the same spirometry tests according to ATS/ERS criteria. The model interpreted each spirometry test on three separate occasions for assessing reproducibility. Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), were calculated by comparing LLM assessments with clinician assessments of spirometry test acceptability and interpretation. Results For spirometry acceptability evaluation, ChatGPT demonstrated an overall accuracy of 87% (95% CI: 81%-92%), sensitivity of 91% (95% CI: 85%-95%), specificity of 61% (95% CI 39%-80%), PPV of 94% (95% CI: 89%-97%), and NPV of 48(95% CI: 29%-67%) with Cohen's k of 0.46. The spiromteric interpretation agreement with the clinicians reference standard was moderate, with exact agreement of 0.61 (95% CI: 0.54–0.69) while Cohen's Kappa (Unweighted) was 0.47 (95% CI: 0.37–0.56) and Macro F1 score was 0.39 (95% CI: 0.33–0.49). Reproducibility across three independent trials was moderate (Fleiss’ κ 0.58). Class-specific interpretation performance varied by category; sensitivity was highest for normal pattern and restrictive defects (0.72), whereas sensitivity for obstructive defects was 0.27. F1-scores were highest for normal and restrictive defects (0.81 and 0.62, respectively). Conclusion The current findings suggest that ChatGPT 5.5 has a limited capability, at its current stage of development, to serve as a reliable tool for independent spirometry interpretation in clinical practice. Nevertheless, it may serve as an adjunct to clinical decision-making and educational tools. Prospective controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings.

items.title: Accuracy, reproducibility, and concordance of ChatGPT and Gemini on text-based questions from the Turkish Orthopaedics and Traumatology Board Examination: a multi-year comparative study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Data on the reproducibility, shared error patterns, and multi-year performance of large language models (LLMs) on national orthopaedic board examinations are limited. This study compared the accuracy, response reproducibility, explanation quality, and inter-model concordance of ChatGPT and Gemini on text-based questions from the Turkish Orthopaedics and Traumatology Board Examination (TOTBE), with exploratory benchmarking against published examination statistics. Methods Of 500 TOTBE questions administered between 2021 and 2025, 52 image-based and one annulled question were excluded, leaving 447 text-based questions. Each question, presented in its original Turkish language, was submitted twice to ChatGPT 5.2 (OpenAI) and Gemini 3 Flash (Google) via their public interfaces on January 20 and January 27, 2026, yielding 1,788 responses. Primary analyses used the first response at the question level; second responses served for reproducibility assessment and an additional sensitivity analysis, and a generalized estimating equation (GEE) model accounted for within-question correlation. Accuracy was compared using the exact McNemar test. Two orthopaedic surgeons independently rated explanation quality on a 5-point Likert scale (inter-rater reliability, ICC(2,1)). Results ChatGPT answered 377 of 447 questions correctly (84.34%; 95% CI, 80.68–87.41) and Gemini 396 of 447 (88.59%; 95% CI, 85.31–91.21); Gemini was significantly more accurate ( p = 0.011). Reproducibility was excellent for both models (ChatGPT 94.41%, κ = 0.930; Gemini 97.32%, κ = 0.966). Of 35 questions missed by both models, 25 (71.4%) involved the same incorrect option. The GEE analysis confirmed higher odds of a correct response for Gemini (OR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.10–1.89; p = 0.008). Explanation quality did not differ significantly ( p = 0.065). Both models exceeded the published passing thresholds in every year. Conclusions Contemporary LLMs achieved high accuracy and excellent reproducibility on text-based TOTBE questions, with Gemini demonstrating significantly higher first-attempt accuracy than ChatGPT. To our knowledge, this is the first study to evaluate accuracy, reproducibility, and inter-model concordance together across multiple years of a national orthopaedic board examination. Because only the text-based component was evaluated under non-equivalent testing conditions, the findings should not be interpreted as evidence of overall orthopaedic competence or as direct comparisons with human examinees. Clinical trial number Not applicable. Level of evidence Level IV Diagnostic/Methodological Study (retrospective).

items.title: ActICL: Post-Training for Agentic Multimodal In-Context Learning
items.abstract: Multimodal in-context learning (ICL) is an important capability of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). Its performance is closely tied to the demonstrations it uses, making demonstration retrieval a core problem for ICL. Common methods use fixed scoring methods to retrieve all the demonstrations at once, which may introduce redundancy and noise. Context-aware retrieval methods have emerged to address this problem by allowing incremental retrieval from a growing context. However, none of them lets the MLLM learn how to judge what new demonstrations it needs and then carry out progressive retrieval on its own. To this end, we introduce ActICL, which trains an MLLM agent to acquire and use an ICL context via tool-augmented reasoning. An ActICL agent analyzes its own information gaps during iterative reasoning and tool-use actions. Based on these gaps, it performs targeted retrieval to acquire a set of initial candidates. It can then use the existing context to further filter the candidates and refine the context, or it can iteratively perform a new retrieval. When the agent judges that the context is sufficient for the task, or when the resource limit is reached with the user request met, it sends the acquired context to an answering model, either the agent itself or another MLLM. We use a two-stage post-training procedure that jointly optimizes the agent's acquisition and answering. With an adaptive number of demonstrations, ActICL improves average performance by 11.6 percentage points over standard similarity-based retrieval across seven benchmarks and three MLLMs, and by 4.4 points compared to the strongest prior baseline. The contexts acquired by ActICL agents can also be used effectively by frontier models. When GPT-5.6-Sol performs 4-shot ICL, ActICL's contexts improve its performance by 3.5 points over standard retrieval, averaged over three benchmarks.

items.title: ActMOF: Mapping Reticular Synthesis through Active Learning
items.abstract: Reticular chemistry allows metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) to be designed from their building units, yet their synthesis remains constrained by sparse experimental data, noisy crystallization outcomes, and the absence of benchmarks for comparing active-learning strategies. While data-driven approaches such as Bayesian optimization (BO) can improve synthesis success rates, selecting appropriate optimizers beforehand for mapping MOF crystallization landscapes remains largely empirical. Here we present ActMOF, an experiment-grounded benchmark for comparing search strategies in aluminum-carboxylate MOF synthesis. ActMOF is emulated from experimentally measured microwave syntheses with each encoded condition assigned a crystallinity index calculated based on diffraction peak intensity and full width at half-maximum. By benchmarking policies guided by Gaussian processes (GP), tree ensembles and large language models (LLM), ActMOF placed the GP family among the leading policies for active learning in sparse synthesis landscapes. It then demonstrated transferability by guiding the microwave synthesis of six reticularly related aluminum MOFs. All six campaigns gave crystalline products within a fixed budget of 12 experiments each, and established a reusable testbed for AI-driven MOF synthesis.

items.title: Adapting large language models for urban trip purpose inference: A domain-informed textual representation and fine-tuning framework
items.abstract: Understanding why people travel is fundamental to activity-based travel demand modelling and transport policy analysis. However, conventional trip purpose inference methods typically represent mobility contexts using predefined numerical or categorical features, which may discard semantic information contained in raw contextual data, thereby limiting their ability to represent and distinguish diverse travel-related contexts. To address this gap, this study proposes TripPurpose LLM, a domain-informed trip purpose inference framework based on large language models (LLMs). The framework integrates traveller attributes, departure time, transport mode, and semantic information from nearby points of interest (POIs) into a unified textual representation, incorporates transport domain knowledge through structured chain-of-thought (CoT) guidance, and adapts pretrained LLMs using low-rank adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning. Experiments used 10,513 survey-based trip records from Guangzhou, China. Within the TripPurpose LLM framework, retaining the original POI names increased the accuracy of Qwen3-8B from 0.695 to 0.745 and its Macro-F1 from 0.610 to 0.681, with both metrics exceeding those of structured-feature machine-learning baselines and classifiers using term frequency–inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) features or fixed MacBERT embeddings. This finding highlights the value of contextual semantic modelling for trip purpose inference. Across ten LLM backbones, TripPurpose LLM combining LoRA fine-tuning with CoT guidance consistently achieved the strongest performance among the evaluated settings, with accuracy ranging from 0.71 to 0.76. This pattern demonstrates the framework's effectiveness across different model families and parameter scales. This study provides an integrative framework for inferring trip purposes from travel records, thereby supporting travel-demand analysis, transport planning, and policy evaluation.

items.title: Advances in artificial intelligence for brain imaging and computer-aided diagnosis of neurological diseases: a systematic literature review
items.abstract: Background Brain imaging is central to the structural, functional, metabolic, and neurophysiological characterization of neurological disease, yet interpretation remains constrained by heterogeneity in acquisition, annotation, expertise, and clinical context. Objective This systematic literature review evaluates recent artificial intelligence approaches for brain imaging and computer-aided diagnosis, with emphasis on methods, modalities, neurological diseases, diagnostic tasks, datasets, validation practices, and translational limitations. Methods The review followed PRISMA 2020 and covered peer-reviewed English-language studies published from January 2020 through June 2026. Eight information sources were searched using database-specific terms for artificial intelligence, neuroimaging, neurological disease, and diagnostic analysis. The search identified 1,078 records; 236 duplicates were removed, 842 unique records were screened, 258 full texts were assessed, and 123 studies were included after a record-level eligibility re-audit. Heterogeneous evidence was synthesized narratively and by descriptive mapping rather than meta-analysis. Results MRI was frequently represented in the included studies and auxiliary mapping data; CT was commonly used in acute stroke and intracranial hemorrhage; PET supported selected molecular and differential-diagnosis studies; fMRI and diffusion imaging were used for network and white-matter analysis; and EEG extended the scope to neurophysiological diagnosis. CNN and three-dimensional networks were commonly reported, while attention, Transformer, graph, self-supervised, generative, multimodal, and foundation-model approaches appeared in selected recent studies. Stroke, dementia, and brain tumors were frequently represented, but heterogeneous populations, outcomes, and incomplete validation extraction precluded ranking diseases, modalities, architectures, or validation strategies. Conclusion The evidence suggests movement from task-specific pattern recognition toward multimodal and context-rich decision support in selected settings, but it does not establish uniform methodological superiority or clinical maturity. Dependable translation requires patient-level data governance, transparent reporting, uncertainty estimation, independent multicenter testing, prospective workflow evaluation, and clinically meaningful endpoints.

items.title: Advances in Interventional Oncology for Hepatocellular Carcinoma
items.abstract: Locoregional therapies are used across the hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) treatment spectrum, including for curative treatment of small tumors, as bridging or downstaging therapy before liver transplant, for treatment of intermediate-stage disease, and as part of combination treatment with systemic therapy in selected patients. This narrative review summarizes recent developments in transarterial radioembolization (TARE), transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), and percutaneous ablation techniques and separates established clinical advances from early investigational work. The strongest evidence supports personalized TARE dosimetry and radiation segmentectomy, selective TACE with reassessment before repeat treatment, and image-guided thermal ablation with objective margin assessment. Phase 3 trials of TACE combined with antiangiogenic and immune checkpoint therapy demonstrated improved progression-free survival in selected patients with unresectable, nonmetastatic HCC, although the survival benefit of these combinations so far extends only to progression-free survival, and the best treatment sequence remains to be defined. Histotripsy, pulsed electric-field ablation, electrochemotherapy, cryoablation, high-intensity focused ultrasound, imageable or alternative radioembolic microspheres, new embolic agents, robotics, and artificial intelligence remain at different stages of clinical development. Most supporting data are derived from single-arm studies, retrospective cohort studies, trials in mixed liver-tumor populations, or studies in preclinical models. Treatment selection should account for tumor burden and location, liver function, portal hypertension, vascular invasion, transplant candidacy, available alternatives, local expertise, and patient preferences. Future studies should focus on durable local control, preservation of liver function, quality of life, transplant eligibility, overall survival, and cost.

items.title: Advancing multidimensional enterprise risk management with artificial intelligence
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a conceptual framework designed to assist organizations in understanding and promoting the adoption of a multidimensional Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) enterprise risk management (ERM) that integrates artificial intelligence (AI). The proposed framework serves as a tool to improve organizational risk governance, stability, and resilience within an evolving digital landscape characterized by increasingly complex, rapidly changing, and interdependent risks. Design/methodology/approach This study creates a conceptual framework by expanding upon the conventional technology-organization-environment (TOE) model through theoretical integration and tailored ERM contextualization. The methodology includes an extensive review and synthesis of literature on COSO ERM, multidimensional risk perspectives, AI-driven risk management, and technology adoption frameworks. Findings This paper conceptually extends the TOE framework by maintaining its core dimensions while introducing two novel ERM-specific constructs: security and privacy (SnP) and organizational multidimensional risk–technology awareness (ORTA). It also reconceptualizes three existing TOE constructs to better align with COSO ERM realities: organizational compatibility is embedded within organizational readiness (ORD), top management support is operationalized as tone at the top (TtT), and cost is reframed as value for money (VfM). These additions and refinements enhance the explanatory power of the original TOE framework by demonstrating how both traditional and ERM-specific factors shape organizational perceptions of readiness, trust, and strategic alignment in a digital risk environment. Research limitations/implications The proposed framework improves our theoretical understanding of ERM transformation in the digital era by providing a more integrated explanation of how adoption decisions are shaped within complex governance environments. Unlike previous fragmented explanations of technology uptake, this framework demonstrates how interconnected determinants simultaneously influence ERM transformation, especially in AI-enabled settings. Practical implications From a managerial perspective, the framework offers a structured approach for evaluating adoption readiness and designing interventions that facilitate successful COSO ERM transformation. It allows risk leaders to systematically assess internal preparedness across key governance and capability dimensions, with a particular focus on the awareness of multidimensional risk, leadership commitment, and organizational trust in AI-enabled risk systems. Social implications This study has broader societal implications by promoting stronger organizational resilience and more effective risk governance in an increasingly complex and interconnected world. Adopting a multidimensional COSO ERM integrating AI can enhance an organization's ability to anticipate and respond to emerging risks, including financial, operational, cyber, and ESG-related challenges. Originality/value This study addresses an important gap in the literature by investigating the organizational adoption of a multidimensional COSO ERM integrating AI. The interplay between ERM-specific determinants, technological enablers, and managerial adoption intentions in this context remains largely unexplored. By expanding the TOE framework with novel and refined ERM-focused constructs (e.g. ORTA, ORD, VfM, TtT, and SnP), the proposed conceptual model offers a theoretically robust and practically applicable tool for understanding how organizations address strategic, cultural, and governance challenges in digitalized risk management.

items.title: Advancing subseasonal forecasting with machine learning
items.abstract: Decision-makers rely on weather forecasts to plant crops, manage wildfires, allocate water and energy and prepare for weather extremes1–3. Today, such forecasts enjoy unprecedented accuracy as far as 2 weeks thanks to steady advances in physics-based dynamical models and data-driven artificial intelligence models4–10. However, model skill drops precipitously at subseasonal timescales (2–6 weeks ahead) due to compounding errors, systemic model biases and the chaotic nature of the atmosphere11–15. To counter this degradation, we introduce probabilistic bias correction, a machine learning framework that substantially reduces systematic error by learning to correct historical probabilistic forecasts. When applied to the leading dynamical and artificial intelligence models from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), probabilistic bias correction doubles the modest subseasonal skill of the AI Forecasting System16 and improves the skill of the operationally debiased dynamical model17 for 91% of pressure, 92% of temperature and 98% of precipitation targets. We designed probabilistic bias correction for operational deployment, and, in the 2025 real-time forecasting competition of ECMWF18, its global forecasts were the best for all weather variables and lead times, outperforming the dynamical models from six operational forecasting centres, an international dynamical multimodel ensemble, the AI Forecasting System of ECMWF and the forecasting systems of 34 teams worldwide. These probabilistic skill gains translate into more accurate prediction of extreme events and have the potential to improve agricultural planning, energy management and disaster preparedness in vulnerable communities19. The AI framework probabilistic bias correction is shown to correct weather forecast errors 2 to 6 weeks ahead and boost forecast skill, making it promising for improved extreme-weather prediction.

items.title: Advising the Future
items.abstract: This chapter examines the emergence of artificial intelligence–mediated advising in Indian higher education through the lens of digital empathy. It explores how technological systems are reshaping mentorship, accountability, and student well-being, situating India's experience within a comparative global framework. The analysis combines normative critique focusing on rights, ethics, and justice with empirical grounding derived from policy documents, institutional practices, and international case studies. Drawing on theories of care ethics, sociotechnical systems, and the capability approach, the chapter identifies a value–practice gap in current AI deployments. It argues that empathy must be embedded institutionally rather than simulated algorithmically. Comparative evidence from Finland, Singapore, the United Kingdom, and the United States demonstrates that human-centered governance and transparent design foster trust and inclusion.

items.title: AdvRoNIDS: A Constraint-Aware Framework for Adversarially Robust Network Intrusion Detection via Min-Max Training and Attribution Analysis
items.abstract: Machine learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) have become critical security infrastructure, but the vast majority of published research reports accuracy only on clean, unperturbed traffic, leaving their robustness to adversarial evasion unexplored. Existing research into adversarial robustness, when it has occurred, has largely imported image-domain approaches of unconstrained perturbation to network traffic, producing "adversarial" examples that could not possibly occur on a real network, and so failing to probe the true robustness of the system to real-world adversaries. We propose AdvRoNIDS, a constraint-aware adversarial robustness framework for NIDS that (i) trains a deep 1D-CNN classifier on flow-based features from the CICIDS2017 benchmark, (ii) crafts adversarial examples using the Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) and Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) restricted to a feasibility-constrained perturbation set (ПЅ) respecting feature immutability, non-negativity of cumulative counters, and empirical feature bounds, (iii) hardens the classifier through min-max adversarial training against this constrained attacker, and (iv) evaluates the resulting system using a transparent two-number benchmark of clean accuracy and accuracy-under-attack across a full perturbation-budget sweep. The undefended classifier collapses from 90.45% clean accuracy to 25.11% under realistic constrained attack at ε = 0.10, while the adversarially trained classifier retains 87.96% accuracy under the same attack, a 62.85 percentage-point improvement, with negligible cost to clean accuracy (90.45% to 90.86%). A SHAP-based attribution-drift analysis further demonstrates that this robustness arises mechanistically rather than incidentally: the undefended model's decision attribution shifts drastically under attack (mean drift 1.898), while the robust model's attribution remains substantially more stable (mean drift 0.923), a 51.4% reduction that is statistically significant (Mann-Whitney p<1.87×10⁻¹⁶¹,Cliff's δ = 0.70, a large effect). We additionally present an applied explainability and LLM-assisted incident-triage layer that translates the system's outputs into analyst-readable incident narratives. This work explicitly scopes itself to constrained feature-space robustness, leaving end-to-end packet-level attack realizability for future work.

items.title: Affective and cognitive resources for engagement in AI-assisted language learning: A self-determination theory perspective integrating SEM and random forest
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping language learning in higher education, yet students’ engagement in AI-assisted language learning depends on more than access to technological tools. Drawing on Self-Determination Theory (SDT) as an overarching theoretical perspective, this study examined how emotional intelligence and metacognition were associated with engagement directly and indirectly through enjoyment and self-efficacy, while also evaluating their predictive value. Survey data from 847 university students in China were analyzed using structural equation modeling and random forest analysis with repeated nested cross-validation. The SEM results showed that emotional intelligence and metacognition were positively associated with engagement, enjoyment, and self-efficacy, while enjoyment and self-efficacy were also positively related to engagement. All four indirect effects were significant. The extended random forest model achieved an out-of-sample R² of .472, improving R² by .081 over the baseline random forest and by .069 over the extended linear model. Emotional intelligence showed the highest permutation importance and revealed potentially nonlinear predictive patterns across individual learners. These findings highlight the complementary value of explanatory and predictive approaches for understanding engagement in AI-assisted language learning.

items.title: Agentic Delegation as a Project: Toward a Project Management Framework for Agentic AI
items.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence extends delegation across networks of human and artificial agents. Research already examines delegated authority, autonomy, trust, accountability and coordination. This article addresses a complementary methodological question: how can agentic delegation, considered as a whole, be governed as a project? Drawing on established project management methodologies, including the Project Management Body of Knowledge, PRINCE2 and ISO 21502, the paper examines the transposition of project initiation, stakeholder identification, scope definition, planning, resource management, risk assessment, monitoring, change control, acceptance and closure. Particular attention is given to delegated autonomy, successive sub-delegations, alignment, semantic continuity and the preservation of governing constraints. The Agentic Delegation Charter is proposed as an adaptation of the conventional project charter, established at initiation as the constitutive reference for the delegation project. The paper advances a conceptual and methodological framework rather than an empirically validated governance model. Its limitations and directions for future evaluation are explicitly identified.

items.title: Agentic Influence Operations: A Multi-Dimensional Governance Framework for Generative AI-Enabled Information Disorder in Multimedia Ecosystems
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), synthetic media, social bots, and agentic AI are turning information disorder from a content-verification problem into a governance problem for multimedia information ecosystems. Research on fake news, deepfakes, GenAI misuse, and cyber-enabled influence has developed in largely separate streams, and none of these streams offers an integrated governance model for influence activity coordinated through AI-supported workflows. This study develops such a model through a structured evidence synthesis of 35 peer-reviewed sources published between 2019 and 2026, identified through four structured discovery queries and citation chaining and appraised with evidence-type-specific criteria. The synthesis identifies five mechanisms through which AI reshapes information disorder: influence orchestration, ambiguity production, selective persuasion, hybrid human–machine dissemination, and a trust paradox in countermeasures. On this basis, the study defines agentic influence operations as workflow-level risks and organizes them in a twelve-dimension framework that links AI capabilities, content modality, platform infrastructure, data access, evidentiary trust, organizational harm, and governance control points. It also sets out construct boundary conditions, five propositions with explicit evidence status, a managerial control set, and a phased implementation roadmap. Only the proposition on synthetic media and uncertainty about authentic evidence has direct empirical support; the others are offered for testing through simulation, experimental, design-science, and expert-validation studies.

items.title: AgentSafeEvo: Adversarial Co-Evolution for LLM Agent Safety
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents accomplish complex tasks through multi-turn interactions with external tools. However, malicious content embedded in user queries, tool descriptions, or environment observations can manipulate their decisions and induce unsafe actions. Adversarial co-evolution has emerged as an effective approach to strengthening LLM safety, but existing work primarily focuses on language-level safety or indirect prompt injection in web tasks. In this paper, we introduce AgentSafeEvo, a co-evolutionary reinforcement learning framework for agent safety built on an attacker-defender game spanning diverse tasks and attack types. The attacker learns to construct adversarial agent tasks that expose weaknesses in the defender's tool use, while the defender learns to complete tasks safely under these attacks. We further introduce learnability-guided task weighting, which uses within-task defender-reward variability to adjust each task's contribution to attacker and defender updates. Extensive experiments on agent safety and general capability benchmarks demonstrate that our method improves adversarial robustness while maintaining general agent capabilities.

items.title: AI Agents and Agentic AI: What Sets Them Apart?
items.abstract: The distinction between AI agents and agentic AI is conceptually defensible when it separates an entitythat acts, the properties of its behavior, and the system that enables goal completion. However, theliterature and providers do not establish a universal boundary between two technologies. An agent cancarry out extended processes, and an agentic system can contain a single agent. This article examinesacademic antecedents, contrasts recent taxonomies, and compares terminology used by OpenAI,Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and other providers. It offers an explicitly non-consensus teachingframework and explains why autonomy, agent count, content generation, learning, and authority shouldbe analyzed separately. items.title: AI Agents in Decentralised Social Networks: A Quasi-Experimental Field Study on Behavioural and Structural Dynamics in Farcaster
items.abstract: Why can similarly configured AI agents amplify engagement in some communities yet mainly redirect it in others? We deployed two autonomous AI agents in separate Farcaster channels (January–February 2026) across two incentive phases: Phase 1 with $Degen token rewards and Phase 2 with social recognition through agent follow-backs and mutual-follow encouragement. In /replyors (71 daily replies at baseline, Attention Saturation Ratio 1.17), the difference-in-differences (DiD)-adjusted engagement lift was +228% in Phase 1 and +118% in Phase 2, consistent with engagement amplification, although the seven-day baseline does not establish parallel pre-treatment trends cleanly. In /degen (244 daily replies, ASR 2.17), the channel-level DiD estimate was +18% (p = 0.71) and not statistically distinguishable from zero despite strong topic-level participation. Because the available /degen–/base control is poorly matched on baseline scale and ASR, that comparison is treated as suggestive rather than a clean causal estimate. Phase 1 generated 967 participant reply messages from 61 unique individuals and 101,980 $Degen distributed. Using historical DEGEN/USD closes at the beginning and end of the 9–22 January reward phase as a broad valuation bracket, the aggregate token budget was on the order of US$111–152; this is not a transaction-time weighted valuation. After token removal, participant reply volume within agent-initiated threads fell by approximately 82–90% and Phase 1 participant retention was 27–34%. We introduce the Contextual Amplification Framework (CAF) and Attention Saturation Ratio (ASR) as provisional, exploratory constructs derived from two treated channels. The evidence is consistent with the possibility that pre-existing attention saturation moderates agent effects, but the ASR is not a validated screening rule and requires multi-site replication. The findings carry implications for platform economics, AI governance, and token incentive design.
